It says the state will keep complete equality
Of social and political rights
To all its inhabitants, irrespective of religion, race, or sex.
It says it will safeguard the holy places of all religions.
It says it will be faithful to the principles of the {{x|Charter}}.
The closing words put trust in the {{c|Rock of Israel}}.
The words can be heard as God.
The words can be heard as the people.
The text does not say which.

The {{x|Arab}} state in the plan was not declared.
On the fifteenth the armies entered:
{{p|Egypt}}, {{p|Transjordan}}, {{p|Syria}}, {{p|Lebanon}}, and {{p|Iraq}}.
{{p|Transjordan}} is the name that state then used.
{{p|Jerusalem}} was not set up as the separated city.
The fighting divided it.
The international regime was not established.

People left their houses.
People were driven from their houses.
The counts of how many do not agree.
This chapter does not choose a count.
Neither fact cancels the other.
A village is not the whole, and the whole is not a village.
The {{p|United States}} recognized the state that day,
De facto.
Recognition is not the map.

Do not say the recommendation was the country.
The {{x|Assembly}} drew three regimes on one land.
What the year did was one declaration, a war,
And a city that was not international.
Do not say the scroll's equality is a report of the year.
It is a charge the state wrote down for itself.
A charge is not kept by being written.
Do not say the war was the only answer the vote could have had.
Do not say the vote was nothing because a war followed.
The {{x|Agency}} said yes. The {{x|Committee}} said no.
Those were decisions. Other decisions were open,
And were not taken.

Hold the three lines the plan drew,
And the one state the scroll declared,
And the houses the year emptied, by leaving and by driving.
Refuse the consolation that a resolution is a birth,
And the consolation that a birth erases the resolution's other state.
The striving named in the scroll is equality,
And the holy places of all religions, kept.
The year did not accomplish the sentence.
The sentence remains a sentence.
Count the vote on the twenty-ninth of November.
Count the scroll on the fourteenth of May.
The map of the plan and the map of the fighting
Are not the same map.


# Chapter 321: The Suggested Copy

On the twenty-fifth of April, 1953, the journal {{x|Nature}}
Printed three papers on one substance.
The substance is deoxyribose nucleic acid.
The initials are DNA.
The first paper is from {{p|Cambridge}}.
{{c|James Watson}} and {{c|Francis Crick}} wrote it.
They wish to suggest a structure.
Two chains, wound together.
The bases pair.
Adenine fits thymine.
Guanine fits cytosine.
The paper says it has not escaped their notice
That the pairing they have postulated
Immediately suggests a possible copying mechanism
For the genetic material.
They say the suggestion was stimulated
By the unpublished results and ideas
Of workers in {{p|London}}.
A suggestion is not a measurement they made.
It begins on one page and ends on the next.

The other two papers are from {{p|King's College}}, {{p|London}}.
{{c|Maurice Wilkins}} and his colleagues signed one.
{{c|Rosalind Franklin}} and {{c|Raymond Gosling}} signed the other.
Their photograph of the salt, taken in 1952,
Is in that issue under their names.
{{c|Franklin}} had measured a helix.
She had the phosphates on the outside
And the bases toward the middle.
She had not signed the {{p|Cambridge}} page.
Do not say she failed to see her own photograph.
The claim that she missed it is a later telling.
The journal of that April prints her name
On the evidence.

In 1968 {{c|Watson}} published a book.
He wrote that {{c|Wilkins}} showed him the photograph
In the first months of 1953,
And that his pulse raced.
The book is his account, fifteen years on.
It is not the issue of the journal.
The book speaks of her in a way the April page does not.
Take the page.

Five weeks later, on the thirtieth of May,
{{c|Watson}} and {{c|Crick}} published the genetical implications.
The April sentence had already said the pairing suggests a copy.

This was not the discovery of the substance.
The substance had a name long before.
In 1944 {{c|Oswald Avery}}, with {{c|Colin MacLeod}}
And {{c|Maclyn McCarty}}, had shown that a substance
Which changed what a bacterium would be
Was this acid, and not a protein.
The year before the April papers,
{{c|Alfred Hershey}} and {{c|Martha Chase}}
Had argued that what a virus puts into a bacterium,
The part that carries the change, is the acid
And not the coat.
The April page is a structure.
It is not the first news that the acid can carry a heredity.

{{c|Erwin Chargaff}} had weighed the bases.
Adenine matched thymine.
Guanine matched cytosine.
The model uses that match.
He did not sign the April papers.
Earlier in 1953 {{c|Linus Pauling}} had published a structure
Of three chains.
It did not hold.
The {{p|Cambridge}} page says its own structure is another.

In 1962 the prize in physiology or medicine
Went to {{c|Watson}}, to {{c|Crick}}, and to {{c|Wilkins}}.
{{c|Franklin}} had died in 1958.
The prize is not given to the dead.
Her name is on the April page.
The prize's list is not that page.
Do not move the prize back into the month of the papers.
Do not make the later book the judge of what she measured.

A pairing is a finite means.
One chain can set the bases of the next.
The setting is a copy, if the fit holds.
The fit does not say whether the copy should be made.
The fit does not say what the copy is for.
Do not make the page into a verdict on a life.
Do not make the copying into a permission.
The paper says suggests.
It says possible.
Hold those two words.
They are the paper's own care.

Count the twenty-fifth of April.
Count three papers, and whose name is on each.
Count the thirtieth of May as the implications,
Not as the first sentence.
The substance was already known to carry a change.
The new sentence is the shape, and the copy the shape allows.
A shape is not a commandment.
The dead of the prize's year are not this chapter.
{{c|Franklin}}'s measurement is.


# Chapter 322: The Published Frequency

On the fourth of October, 1957, at twenty-eight minutes
And thirty-four seconds past seven in the evening,
By the time kept at {{p|Greenwich}},
A sphere left a pad at {{p|Tyuratam}}.
By the clock in {{p|Moscow}} it was twenty-eight minutes
And thirty-four seconds past ten at night.
At the pad it was twenty-eight minutes
And thirty-four seconds past midnight,
And the date was the fifth.
Do not collapse the three clocks into one day.
The world dates the launch on the fourth.

The pad is in what is now {{p|Kazakhstan}}.
The site is now called {{p|Baikonur}}.
The town of that name is not the pad.
Do not say the sphere left from the town.

The sphere was the simplest satellite.
The word in the announcement is the word for a satellite.
The name that stayed is {{x|Sputnik}}.
It was fifty-eight centimeters across.
It weighed 83.6 kilograms.
Four antennas stood out from it.
Thirty-six bolts joined the shell.
Nitrogen was sealed inside.
These are the object's measures.
They are not a meaning.

The rocket was a form of the {{x|R-7}}.
That form had been made to carry a warhead
From one continent to another.
In August of that year a rocket of this form
Had already completed a flight, with no satellite on it.
This one carried a sphere.
The sphere was not a bomb.
Do not make the orbit into a proof
That a weapon had been justified.
Do not make the sphere into the weapon.

{{c|Sergei Korolev}} directed the work.
The state did not publish his name.
The frequency was published.
Hold those two acts.
They are not the same kind of secrecy.

The sphere transmitted on 20.005
And on 40.002.
A beep, and a beep.
A radio that could reach those numbers
Could hear that the sphere was passing.
The beep is not a speech.
It says the body is there.
It does not say why the body was sent.

That night the agency announced
That a satellite was in orbit.
A circuit takes about ninety-six minutes.
The announcement is not the beep.

The batteries lasted until the twenty-sixth of October.
On the fourth of January, 1958, the sphere came down.
It burned. It was not recovered.
The counts of its circuits do not agree.
No count is chosen.

On the third of November a second satellite
Left the same pad.
It carried a dog. Her name was {{c|Laika}}.
There was no way prepared to bring her down.
The report said she lived for days.
In 2002 {{c|Dimitri Malashenkov}} said the heat
Had killed her within hours,
By the fourth circuit.
Do not repeat the report that she lived for days.
Do not describe the cabin.
She was sent, and she was not brought back.
The seventh of November was the anniversary
They were writing toward.
The dog went up on the third.
An anniversary is not a reason that answers for her.

This day of the book keeps a rite on the fifteenth of November,
In the count {{p|Japan}} uses.
The rite is {{x|Shichi-go-san}}.
Seven, five, and three.
It is not a holiday of the state.
A household may go on the day, or on a day near it.

At three the child's hair was let grow.
That rite was kept for girls and for boys.
At five a boy was dressed in hakama,
The formal trousers.
At seven a girl took the wide sash.
The visit to a shrine, as households keep it,
Spread in the {{x|Meiji}} years.
Do not say a shogun fixed the fifteenth.
That story is told, and it is not settled.

The child is taken to a shrine.
Thanks are given that the child has lived.
The wish is that the child go on living.
The candy is called a thousand years.
It is red and white.
The candy is not a contract.

Do not say the children were brought
Because a sphere was in the sky.
The year of the launch is 1957.
The rite is older than the year.
The calendar of this book puts them on one day.
Count both. Do not make them one cause.

A frequency can say that a body is passing.
It cannot say whether the body should have been sent.
A count of three ages can say a child has lived this far.
It cannot say the child will live a thousand years.
The rocket was built for a warhead.
The night it flew, it carried a sphere that beeped.
The beep is a finite means.
The rite is a finite thanks.
Neither one is a permission.
Neither one is the sky's purpose.

Count the fourth of October by the world's clock,
And the fifth at the pad.
Count the name that was withheld
And the two numbers that were not.
Count the dog, and the hours, not the days.
Count seven, five, and three.
The sphere came down.
The rite is still kept.


# Chapter 323: The Mother Tongue

On the eleventh of October, 1962,
In the basilica of {{c|Saint Peter}}, in {{p|Vatican City}},
{{c|John XXIII}} opened a council.
He had said, on the twenty-fifth of January, 1959,
In {{p|Rome}}, to the cardinals gathered in the house
Beside the basilica of {{p|Saint Paul Outside the Walls}},
That a council would be called,
And a synod for the city,
And a bringing up to date of the code of the law.
The word on the code was aggiornamento.
It means a bringing up to date.
It was not the name of the council.

The first session closed on the eighth of December.
He died on the third of June, 1963, in {{p|Rome}}.
The council was between its sessions.
He did not promulgate the constitution on the rite.

{{c|Paul VI}} was elected on the twenty-first of June.
The second session ran from the twenty-ninth of September
To the fourth of December, 1963.
On that day he promulgated the constitution
On the sacred liturgy.
Its name is {{x|Sacrosanctum Concilium}}.

Particular law remaining in force,
The use of {{x|Latin}} is to be preserved in the {{x|Latin}} rites.
Since the mother tongue, in the {{x|Mass}},
In the sacraments, and in the other parts,
May often be of great advantage to the people,
The limits of its use may be extended.
In the first place, the readings and the directives,
And some of the prayers and the chants.

In Masses celebrated with the people,
A suitable place may be allotted to their mother tongue.
First, the readings and the common prayer.
Also, as the place warrants,
The parts that pertain to the people.
Steps are to be taken so that the same people
May also say, or sing, in {{x|Latin}},
The parts of the ordinary that are theirs.
A use wider than that follows a further article.
It is not taken by the parish.

The competent territorial authority decides the extent.
The {{x|Apostolic See}} confirms the decision.
A translation into the mother tongue
Is made from the {{x|Latin}} text,
And that authority approves it.
No other person, even a priest,
May add, or remove, or change anything in the rite
On his own authority.

The practical norms are for the {{x|Roman rite}}.
The other rites, lawfully acknowledged,
Are held of equal right and dignity,
And are to be preserved.
Particular law had already excepted some places.
The constitution keeps the exception.
The {{x|Kyrie}} of the {{x|Mass}} was already {{x|Greek}}.

On the twenty-sixth of September, 1964,
An instruction carried the constitution toward the Sunday.
The {{x|Consilium}} prepared it, by mandate of {{c|Paul VI}}.
{{c|Giacomo Lercaro}} presented it.
{{c|Paul VI}} confirmed it in an audience
Given to {{c|Arcadio Maria Larraona}},
Prefect of the {{x|Congregation of Rites}},
And ordered it observed from the seventh of March, 1965,
The first Sunday of {{x|Lent}}.

For a {{x|Mass}} with a congregation,
Once the {{x|Holy See}} has confirmed the decision,
The people's language may be used
For the lessons, the epistle, and the gospel,
For the prayer of the faithful,
For the chants of the ordinary,
The {{x|Kyrie}}, the {{x|Gloria}}, the creed,
The {{x|Sanctus}}, and the {{x|Agnus Dei}},
For the introit, the offertory, and the communion,
For the chants between the readings,
For the greetings and the dialogues,
For the words at the people's communion,
And for the {{x|Lord's Prayer}},
With its introduction and the short prayer after it.
The book at the rite keeps the {{x|Latin}} text beside the other.
The pastors are charged to see
That the people can still say, or sing, in {{x|Latin}},
The parts of the ordinary that are theirs.

The parts the priest sings or says alone
Are not on that list.
The {{x|Holy See}} alone can permit those.
Do not say the whole {{x|Mass}} changed its tongue
On the seventh of March.
Do not say the instruction took the priest's own prayer
Out of {{x|Latin}}.

The council closed on the eighth of December, 1965.
The constitution was not a new book of the {{x|Mass}}.
A later book is not moved back into these years.

Do not say the council silenced {{x|Latin}}.
The page that opens the mother tongue
Says that {{x|Latin}} is to be preserved.
Do not say the people were left outside the words.
The constitution says they are not to be there
As strangers, or as silent spectators.
That sentence is a charge.
It is not a report of every parish.
Conscious participation, active participation,
Is called their right and their duty, by baptism.
Hearing a reading is not the whole of the charge.
It is the part the years in this chapter actually opened.

A permission is not yet a Sunday.
Hold the two sentences on the one page.
The striving is that the people understand the rite
And take their part in it,
In a tongue they are given, and in the {{x|Latin}}
The page refused to discard.
Count the constitution on the fourth of December.
Count the instruction on the seventh of March.
In these years the tongue of the reading
And the tongue of the prayer the priest said alone
Were not the same tongue.


# Chapter 324: The Master in the Mountain

The filming did not begin in the year of the vault.
In 1938 the {{x|Genealogical Society of Utah}}
Began to copy books onto rolls of film.
The vault is where the masters were put.
It is not the first camera.

The place is {{p|Little Cottonwood Canyon}},
In the {{p|Wasatch}}, in {{p|Utah}},
About a mile up from the mouth,
About twenty miles southeast of {{p|Salt Lake City}}.
The room is cut into the north wall.
The published depth is about six hundred feet.
The cover of stone over the rooms
Was published as hundreds of feet,
And the numbers do not agree.
No single cover is chosen.
A depth and a cover are not the same measure.

The stone is called granite.
The rock is quartz monzonite.
It is the stone of the temple in the city.
The temple's blocks were split from boulders
At the mouth of the canyon.
The workers' account is that explosives
Were not used on those blocks.
The temple was dedicated in 1893.
The vault was blasted into the wall.
The quarry and the vault are not the same cut.

In the late years of the 1950s the site was tested.
Blasting began in May 1960.
In April 1963 the first rolls were carried in.
The construction was not finished
Until December of that year.
In that December visitors were taken through.
Do not say the mountain was never shown.
The showing is not a reading room.

The published cost was two million dollars.
One account assigns fourteen tons to the main door
And nine tons to each of the two smaller doors.
Another says nine to fourteen tons at a door.
They were said to stand against a blast.
No weight is chosen over the other.
The saying is not a trial this chapter watched.

A laboratory sits under the overhang.
The storage is deeper in.
One account gives six chambers.
A newspaper, at the December showing,
Gave three long corridors and four cross tunnels.
The two descriptions are not forced into one number.
No count of rooms is chosen.

In 1965 the vault was in operation.
It was named in May 1966.
It was dedicated on the twenty-second of June, 1966.
Do not say the whole of it was built in 1965.
1965 is the year the work was going.
The dedication is the next year.

The owner is the {{x|Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints}}.
The society that sent the cameras
Is the {{x|Genealogical Society of Utah}}.
Where an archive agreed, a camera copied the books.
The camera does not take the book.
The book stays where it was.
The film is a copy of the page
As the page was on the day of the filming.

The master roll stays in the mountain.
A person who comes to read
Comes to a copy, elsewhere.
The vault is not that room.

The names are kept so that the living
Can ask a rite for the dead.
The rite named here is a baptism,
Done by a living person, in a temple,
In the name of someone who has died.
The rite is not done in the mountain.
The mountain keeps the name.
The church teaches that the dead
May accept what was asked, or refuse it.
That is the teaching.
It is not a report of any one dead person.
The film does not perform the rite.
The film does not obtain the answer.

Do not say every person who has died
Is in the mountain.
The rolls are the books the cameras reached.
A name not filmed is not invented here.
A later copying onto disks,
And a site on the network,
Are not this year.
Do not move them back.

A film can be copied again
If the book it came from burns.
That is a real keeping.
The same film lays a population open to an office.
A copy is not a consent.
A consent is not a copy.
The striving is that a name not be lost,
And that a rite not be spoken
As if the film had been the will.

Count 1938 as the start of the filming.
Count May 1960 as the start of the blasting.
Count April 1963 as the first rolls,
And December 1963 as the showing.
Count 1965 as the year of the operation.
Count the twenty-second of June, 1966, as the dedication.
The master stays.
The book stays in its archive.
The question the rite asks
Is not answered by the stone.


# Chapter 325: Left as a Museum

On the sixteenth of May, 1966,
A circular went out inside the party, in {{p|Beijing}}.
It was called a notification.
The name that stayed is the {{x|Cultural Revolution}}.
The country was not given the text that day.
{{x|People's Daily}} printed it a year later,
On the seventeenth of May, 1967.
A circular inside a party is not a vote of the people.

On the eighth of August the {{x|Central Committee}} adopted
A decision on that revolution, in sixteen points.
The decision is not a catalog of what to break.

On the first of June the same newspaper had printed four names:
Old ideas, old culture, old customs, old habits.
Which object was old was not written down.
On the eighteenth of August, at the gate in {{p|Beijing}},
{{c|Mao Zedong}} received the {{c|Red Guards}}.
He wore an army coat.
{{c|Lin Biao}} told the crowd to smash the four.
The size of the crowd is not settled in this chapter.
In the days after, the breaking began in the city.
Do not say the four names were a law with edges.
Do not say a name in a newspaper is a stone already fallen.

Temples were broken. Books were burned.
Tablets were smashed. Graves were opened.
People were beaten. People were killed.
The counts of the dead do not agree.
This chapter does not choose a count.
Some objects were hidden.
A hidden book does not put a hall back.
A hall still standing does not close a grave.
A person is not the label the month set on them.
The {{c|Red Guards}} were students.
They were not the whole of the country.

In {{p|Qufu}} the temple, the mansion, and the cemetery
Of {{c|Confucius}} stood under a protection of the state.
In August the hands charged with the three places
Did not give them up.
Early in November a group came from {{p|Beijing}},
Led by {{c|Tan Houlan}}, of {{p|Beijing Normal University}}.
On the twelfth, later accounts give the word
From {{c|Chen Boda}} and {{c|Qi Benyu}} as three charges.
Do not destroy the mansion, the temple, or the cemetery.
Leave them as a museum.
The grave may be dug.
The accounts do not agree on which stones were to be spared.
This chapter keeps the three charges they share.

On the fifteenth the stones that marked the protection
Were broken at a rally.
In the last days of November the grave was dug.
This chapter does not say what the diggers found.
Books were burned.
The counts made afterward do not agree.
This chapter does not choose a count.
Some things were hidden by the people of the place.
The clay of a statue is not the rite.
The rite is not kept by calling the clay only clay.
The grave of the man whose work was the keeping of rites
Was opened under an order that the buildings were to stand.

Do not say the revolution ended tradition.
The order itself said to leave a museum.
A museum is not a sacrifice offered.
Do not say the breaking was nothing,
Because a wall was ordered kept,
Or because a hand hid a book.
The striving is the keeping:
A book, a rite, a grave, a name.
The year opened the grave.
The year did not take every book.
Neither sentence cancels the other.

{{c|Mao Zedong}} died on the ninth of September, 1976,
In {{p|Beijing}}.
On the sixth of October {{c|Hua Guofeng}} had four people arrested:
{{c|Jiang Qing}}, {{c|Zhang Chunqiao}},
{{c|Yao Wenyuan}}, {{c|Wang Hongwen}}.
The name given afterward is the {{c|Gang of Four}}.
The arrest is the end the later telling uses.
It did not fill the grave.
A judgment written in a later year
Is not moved back into this October.

Hold the circular, and the four names,

# Chapter 329: The Covenant of Peace

Proclaim a dawn that crowns the world with light,
The chains of hate lie shattered in the dust.
The crowds arise, and labor claims its right,
From forge and field their hopeful banners thrust.

Yet scarlet suns twice scorched the mourning earth,
Their silent fire wrote horror on the sky;
But hope endured where ash replaced the sand,
And swore that war’s last ember here would die.

A crackling voice on August’s fervent air
Confessed defeat across the empire’s seas;
In {{p|Times Square}} strangers, dazzled, found a dare,
And sealed a vow with one unbridled squeeze.

The second of September set its fate;
Steel decks became the altar of release.
The working world inhaled and sealed its fate,
Proclaiming labor’s covenant of peace.

From {{p|Pittsburgh}} mills to {{p|London}}’s river docks,
The union drums beat loud in molten halls;
Red banners rolled like quick-forged iron shocks,
And bosses felt the tremor in their walls.

{{x|Kartik}} lamps glowed through {{p|India}}’s dark night,
A widow smiled, her children at her side;
As sparks like comets chased the ghosts to flight,
And whispered freedom swelling in the tide.

In ruined fields the {{x|Shintō}} harvest bowed,
White grains were heaped before a broken shrine;
The farmer wept yet offered thanks aloud,
For seeds of hope still quickened in the brine.

In {{p|Nuremberg}} the gavel cracked like doom,
The plague of hate was named before the earth;
Twelve shadows waited judgment in the room,
And heard mankind demand their curse’s birth.

December’s pilgrims gathered on the sand,
Indian scholar singing promised land;
Trader from {{p|Malay}} knelt upon the sand,
Their voices mingled, binding sand to land.

Eight fragile lights renewed a {{p|Warsaw}} room,
The youngest played where once the shadows lay;
Their mother sang against remembered gloom,
And turned the night to promise with her pray.

In ruined towns the bells returned to life,
Their silver peals stitched silence into song;
Young soldiers danced beside a wooden fife,
And swore no tyrant’s reign would last as long.

In {{p|Seoul}} the crowds lit torches in the street,
Their flags proclaimed the empire’s yoke was done;
Yet lines were drawn where foreign soldiers meet,
And dawn arose upon a severed sun.

Across the plains of {{p|China}} drums of peace
Replaced the clash of empire’s hungry blade;
Yet rival banners gathered, never ceased,
And thunder warned of storms that had not fled.

In {{p|Tokyo}} the courtroom lights burned slow,
Two years of witness weighed each mortal crime;
Yet on the throne a sacred ember glowed,
And judgment blurred along the edge of time.

{{x|New Year}}’s decree spoke softly through the gray;
No myth shall bind my people’s hearts at all.
Not akitsumikami, far away,
And trust shall rise, a beacon shared by all.

So ended war and dawned the workers’ dream,
With lamps and bells and grains beneath the sky;
The plague of hate dissolved like distant steam,
And human hands began to build on high.

The signing in the bay was the second of September, a Sunday.

# Chapter 330: The Source Book

No holiday is named for this day.

In April 1990 two agencies published a plan.

With the {{x|Department of Energy}}.

The five years do not ask for the whole book.

{{x|The Times}} of the fourth of October, a Tuesday,

The human genome, as the plan says it, is not a child's name.

Hold the plan of April,

Refuse the consolation that a plan is a sequence,

# Ophiuchus (13宮) - Days 337-364


# Chapter 337: The Middle Hour

Twenty-six chapters, twenty-six years,
From the first year of the century to the year this was written.
The person is {{c|Emma Leonhart}}, who keeps this book.
She was born on the first of {{x|Aquarius}}, in 11996,
The day this book gives to its fifty-seventh chapter.
The month is not her life. It is the years she lived in,
Seen from where she stood in them.
Where she stood is part of what is seen.
The older books of years did the same:
The grand historian wrote his own house into the record,
And the one who wrote of the rise and fall of dynasties
Wrote from the exile he was living in.
This book does not claim their height.
It claims their method.

In 2001 she was five, and then she was in kindergarten.
In her words, she was in kindergarten during {{x|9/11}}.
That is the whole of what she gives for the year,
And it is enough to place the seeing.
A child of five does not read the papers.
The year arrived in her the way years arrive in children:
Later, by being told, and by the grown-ups' faces.
The rest of this chapter is what she was later told.

## The bubble

The year before, the market of the new companies had risen
As if the network were a country with no border and no tax.
The index of those companies peaked in March of 2000,
Above five thousand.
Then it fell, and kept falling through all of this year,
And did not find its floor until the October after.
At the floor it had lost about four parts in five.
Companies that had sold dog food by mail,
Groceries by the click, anything with a dot and a com,
Were closed, and their stock was paper.
{{x|Pets.com}} had closed in the November before.
{{x|Webvan}}, the grocer, failed in July.
The money that had been sure of the future
Found that the future was not yet there to be sold.
The economists later dated a recession
From March to November of this year.
A recession is a date on a chart.
To the people let go, it was not a date.

At the end of the year, on the second of December,
{{x|Enron}} filed for bankruptcy, in {{p|Houston}}.
It had been the seventh largest company in the country by its own reporting.
The reporting was the fraud.
Its auditor, {{x|Arthur Andersen}}, would not survive the next year.
Those who held its stock in their pensions
Lost the pensions.
The fall is the year's; the trials are later pages.

The bubble did not prove the network worthless.
It proved that a price is not a value,
And that the people who called the top a new era
Would call the next one a new era too.

## The open encyclopedia

In the first month of the year an encyclopedia opened
That anyone could change.

{{c|Larry Sanger}} had been writing a digest
Of the reports about the clocks of the year two thousand.
In January 2000 he sent a letter
About a successor to that digest.
{{c|Jimmy Wales}} answered with an encyclopedia,
And asked him to lead it.
He has written that the open encyclopedia was {{c|Wales}}'s idea,
And the money the company's.
The company was {{x|Bomis}}. He names {{c|Jimmy Wales}},
{{c|Tim Shell}}, and {{c|Michael Davis}}.
He arrived in {{p|San Diego}} early in February,
And finished in June the degree the work had asked.

The first book was called {{x|Nupedia}}.
A board of volunteers, most of them with degrees,
Agreed to seven steps before a page was posted.
The first page to pass was on atonality,
By {{c|Christoph Hust}}.
After a year and more, only a few dozen pages had passed.
The counts do not agree, and this chapter does not make them one.

On the second of January, a Tuesday,
He ate with {{c|Ben Kovitz}}
At a Mexican place in {{p|Pacific Beach}}.
{{c|Ben Kovitz}} told him of {{c|Ward Cunningham}}'s pages,
Which anyone could change,
Under a word for quick.
Each of them remembers the idea a little differently.
The two memories are not one sentence.

On the tenth the open pages went up
Under {{x|Nupedia}}'s address.
The board wanted nothing to do with them,
So they took their own name and their own address.
The address opened on the fifteenth, a Monday,
At wikipedia.com.
It was a .com because ads were still in mind.
He wrote to the list: humor me.
Go there and add a little article.
It will take all of five or ten minutes.

By the end of January there were about six hundred pages.
By September the {{x|New York Times}} wrote of some ten thousand,
From {{x|Abba}} to zygote,
And about a hundred volunteers.
A rule was proposed as a joke:
If the rules make you nervous, ignore them.
He set the joke aside later.
The book did not.

{{c|Emma Leonhart}} came to hate this book, in her words,
As one of the biggest haters of it.
Her reason is not the usual one.
The usual complaint is that anyone can write in it,
So it cannot be trusted.
Her complaint is about the work.
In her words, the book is cool in theory,
And in practice it is like {{x|Amway}}.
Selling soap is not the harm.
You can sell soap, make a good living, have a fulfilling life.
The harm is the apparatus around the soap:
An elaborate ideology that says its way is better,
That makes people enthusiastic for the task,
Breaks them, keeps them from getting out,
And takes the labor of people
Who could not do for themselves the thing they wanted.
In her words, the encyclopedia does the same for scholarship.
Being an academic already sucks.
The open book puts a person into a degraded form of it,
With an elaborate justification,
While it extracts free labor,
And the person is nowhere near where they wanted to be in life.
She worked in it, and later in its sister, the book of data,
For years, at a scale few people reach.
Her criticism is from inside.
The book is capable of changing its positions,
And its position on this book may change.
In this edition it is hers.

The five or ten minutes were real.
So were the years they turned into, for some.

## The Taliban and the statues

In {{p|Afghanistan}} the {{x|Taliban}} held most of the country.
In March they destroyed the two great {{x|Buddhas of Bamiyan}},
Carved into the cliff fifteen centuries before.
They used artillery, and then explosives,
Over weeks, while the world asked them to stop
And offered to buy the statues and carry them away.
The empty niches remain.
A thing that has stood for fifteen hundred years
Can be made a hole in a month.

On the ninth of September, two days before the planes,
{{c|Ahmad Shah Massoud}}, who led the last front against them in the north,
Was killed by two men posing as journalists,
With a bomb hidden in their camera.

## The first marriages

On the first of April, at midnight, in {{p|Amsterdam}},
The mayor, {{c|Job Cohen}}, married four couples, men to men and women to women,
Under a law that made the {{p|Netherlands}} the first country
To open marriage to two people of the same sex.
It was not a joke for the first of April.
It was the first of many such days, in many countries,
That this month will count as they come.
A child of five in another country did not know it had happened.
It was happening for her anyway.

## The year's other rooms

On the twentieth of January {{c|George W. Bush}} was sworn in,
After an election settled by the courts the month before.
On the fifteenth and sixteenth of February
Two drafts of the human genome were published,
One by the public consortium, one by a company.
The finished sequence is a later chapter.
On the twenty-third of March the station {{x|Mir}}
Was brought down into the {{p|Pacific}}.
On the twenty-eighth of April {{c|Dennis Tito}}
Paid his own way to the station that replaced it,
The first tourist in orbit.
On the first of June, in {{p|Kathmandu}},
The crown prince of {{p|Nepal}} killed the king, the queen,
And others of his family at dinner, and then himself.
On the fifteenth of June six states founded
The {{x|Shanghai Cooperation Organisation}}.
In {{p|Durban}}, at the end of August,
The world met on racism, and walked out on itself.
On the twenty-third of October {{x|Apple}} sold a music player
That held a thousand songs, and called it the {{x|iPod}}.
On the twenty-fifth {{x|Windows XP}} came out.
On the eleventh of December {{p|China}} joined
The {{x|World Trade Organization}},
And the factories of the next twenty years
Began to be the world's.

## The middle hour

On Tuesday, the eleventh of September,
Four planes were turned.
The first struck the north tower, in {{p|New York}}.
The second struck the south.
The third struck the {{p|Pentagon}}, in {{p|Arlington}}.
The fourth came down in a field near {{p|Shanksville}}.
The people on the fourth plane fought.
The plane did not reach a city.

The south tower fell first.
The north tower fell after.
Close to three thousand were killed that morning.
The counts do not agree, and none is chosen here.
Deaths of later years, from the dust,
Are not this morning.

{{c|George W. Bush}} was with children
In a school in {{p|Sarasota}}
When he was told of the second plane.
The children are not the plot.
On Friday the fourteenth, at the cathedral in {{p|Washington}},
He said, we are here in the middle hour of our grief.
The grief is not a trick.
The use of the grief is not the grief.

On Sunday the sixteenth he said the word crusade,
For the war on terrorism.
His spokesman said he had meant a broad cause.
The word had been said.
On Thursday the twentieth he said
Every nation was with them, or with the terrorists.
He demanded that the men who held {{p|Afghanistan}}
Give up the leaders they were sheltering.
{{c|Osama bin Laden}} was named.

Somewhere in a classroom a girl of five
Was in kindergarten that week.
What she understood of it is hers and is not written here.
The country she grew up in
Was the one that came after that morning,
And she had no memory of the one before.

## The letters

A week after the planes, letters were mailed
With a white powder in them.
They went to news offices in {{p|New York}},
To a tabloid's offices in {{p|Florida}},
And, in October, to two senators in {{p|Washington}}.
The powder was anthrax.
Five people died, and more than a dozen others were sickened.
{{c|Robert Stevens}}, a photo editor in {{p|Boca Raton}}, died first, on the fifth of October.
Postal workers died who had only handled the mail.
For a season people opened their envelopes with gloves.
The letters praised God and threatened the country,
And sounded like the men of the planes.
They were not from them.
Years later the investigators named a scientist
At the army's own laboratory,
Who killed himself before he could be tried.
The naming is a later page.
That the fear was used before the facts were in
Belongs to this one.

## The war

On Sunday the seventh of October
The strikes on {{p|Afghanistan}} began.
{{p|Britain}} was in it with them.
The fighters of the north, {{c|Massoud}}'s men without {{c|Massoud}},
Went forward under the bombers.
{{p|Kabul}} fell on the thirteenth of November.
{{p|Kandahar}}, where the {{x|Taliban}} began, fell in December.
In the mountains of {{x|Tora Bora}}
{{c|Osama bin Laden}} was surrounded, and got away.
At {{p|Bonn}}, on the fifth of December, the factions agreed
On a government, and {{c|Hamid Karzai}} led it from the twenty-second.
The war that began that Sunday lasted twenty years.
Its ending is a chapter of this month, and not this one.

On Friday the twenty-sixth of October
A law was signed, the {{x|Patriot Act}},
That let the state look into more than it had,
Libraries, banks, the lines of the phones.
A law is not a creed.
What it was used for is a later chapter, the year of the leaks.

## The year held

A bubble burst, a book opened, statues were blown out of a cliff,
Two men married in {{p|Amsterdam}},
Four planes were turned, letters carried a poison,
And a war began that would outlast the childhood of the girl in the classroom.
This book does not make them one story.
They are one year, and that is all they share,
Except that she lived in all of them.

The absurdity is a morning pressed into a holy war,
By the ones who sent the planes,
And by the word the answer reached for.
The striving is to keep the dead from being a permission,
To tell the prayer and the order apart,
And to tell a price from a value.
Refuse the consolation that the dead had proved a creed,
And the consolation that the prayer was only politics.
Refuse the consolation that a page anyone can change is already true,
And the consolation that the work given to it free
Was given by people with nothing better to do.


# Chapter 338: The New Coins

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2002 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned six,
And her family moved house.
In her words, she moved houses in 2002, in 2008, and in 2014.
This is the first of the three.
A child does not choose a move. She is moved.
The house before is the first place she remembers being taken from,
And the new one is where the year happened to her.
She has said she does not know what 2002 is.
That is honest, and it is how a year looks from six:
A new house, a new room, a new road to school,
And the world outside, which had changed the September before,
Went on changing without asking her.

## The coins

On the first of January twelve countries of {{p|Europe}}
Put away their own money
And took out the same notes and the same coins.
The mark, the franc, the lira, the drachma, the guilder, the peseta,
Went into drawers and into museums.
The euro had been a unit of account for three years.
Now it was a thing in the hand.
A coin carries a face on one side and a nation on the other,
And the nations kept their own faces on the backs.
The fronts were the same.
Ten years later the same coin nearly broke a continent.
That is a later chapter.

## The camp

On the eleventh of January the first prisoners
Were flown to the naval base at {{p|Guantánamo Bay}}, on {{p|Cuba}},
In orange suits, goggled, hooded, kneeling in the gravel,
And the photograph went around the world.
The base was chosen because it was not the country,
So the country's courts, it was argued, did not reach it.
The camp held hundreds, most never charged.
Some were held for more than twenty years.
A place chosen for being outside the law
Is a confession of what the law would have said.

## The axis

On the twenty-ninth of January {{c|George W. Bush}}
Named three countries an axis of evil:
{{p|Iraq}}, {{p|Iran}}, and {{p|North Korea}}.
The three were not allied with each other.
Two of them had fought a war of eight years.
The word axis was borrowed from the war against fascism,
To lend that war's certainty to this one.
By the autumn the {{x|United Nations}} had passed a resolution
Telling {{p|Iraq}} to let the inspectors back in,
And the war the speech was walking toward
Was the next chapter's.

## The reporter

In January {{c|Daniel Pearl}}, a reporter for the {{x|Wall Street Journal}},
Was taken in {{p|Karachi}} while chasing a story.
In February his killers sent a video of his murder.
He said on it that he was Jewish, and that his father was Jewish.
They made the saying the reason.

## The mountains

In March, in the {{x|Shah-i-Kot}} valley of {{p|Afghanistan}},
The Americans and their allies fought
The largest battle of that war's first years,
And called it {{x|Anaconda}}.
The men they were hunting had already learned to leave.

## The court and the new states

On the first of July the {{x|International Criminal Court}} came into being,
A court for the crimes too large for a nation to try:
Genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes.
Sixty countries had ratified its treaty.
The {{p|United States}} withdrew its signature that May.
On the twentieth of May {{p|East Timor}} became a country,
After centuries under {{p|Portugal}}, decades under {{p|Indonesia}},
And a vote in 1999 for which its people were massacred.
On the ninth of July, in {{p|Durban}},
The {{x|African Union}} replaced the older organization of African states.

## The books that lied

In the summer it was found that {{x|WorldCom}},
The telephone company, had dressed its costs as investments,
Billions of them.
On the twenty-first of July it filed for bankruptcy,
The largest the country had ever seen, larger than {{x|Enron}}'s.
On the thirtieth the president signed a law,
{{x|Sarbanes-Oxley}}, that made the chiefs of companies
Sign their names to their own books.
On the ninth of October the index of the new companies
Found its floor, at about a fifth of its peak.
The bubble of the chapter before was done falling.

## The encyclopedia's first editor leaves

On the first of March {{c|Larry Sanger}}
Left the open encyclopedia he had named.
The company could no longer pay an editor.
The book that anyone could change
Went on without the one who had asked people to change it.
In September of the next year the older book of seven steps was shut down.
The open book had swallowed it.

## The bombs

On the twelfth of October, on {{p|Bali}}, in {{p|Indonesia}},
Bombs went off in two nightclubs in {{p|Kuta}}.
Two hundred and two people were killed,
Most of them tourists, eighty-eight of them from {{p|Australia}}.
The group that did it was tied to the men of the planes.
On the twenty-third of October, in {{p|Moscow}},
Chechen fighters took a theater during a musical,
Some eight hundred and fifty people inside.
On the twenty-sixth the {{x|FSB}} pumped a gas into the hall
And stormed it.
The fighters died, and about a hundred and thirty of the hostages,
Most from the gas, which the state would not fully name
To the doctors trying to save them.
The rescue was the killing.

## The department

In October two men with a rifle in the trunk of a car
Shot people at random around {{p|Washington}} for three weeks.
Ten died.
On the twenty-fifth of November the president signed a law
That made a {{x|Department of Homeland Security}},
Twenty-two agencies under one roof,
The largest change to the government in half a century.
The word homeland had not been a common American word.
It became one.

## The first case

On the sixteenth of November, in {{p|Foshan}}, in {{p|Guangdong}},
A man fell ill with a pneumonia no one could name.
It would be called {{x|SARS}}.
The next spring it would reach thirty countries.
The province said little for months.
This is the year it began, quietly, in a market city.
The great sickness of 2020 is eighteen chapters away,
And its first months will look much the same.

## The year held

A new house for a girl of six.
New coins in twelve countries.
A camp outside the law, an axis that was not an axis,
A court the strongest country would not join,
A new country in {{p|East Timor}}, the largest fraud and bankruptcy yet,
Bombs in {{p|Bali}}, gas in {{p|Moscow}},
A department for the homeland, and a cough in {{p|Foshan}}.
The year between the planes and the invasion
Was the year the invasion was built.
She did not know it was being built.
Hardly anyone her age did.

Refuse the consolation that a place outside the law
Is a place the law cannot see,
And the consolation that a rescue is measured by the hostages taken from the captors
And not by the hostages who lived.


# Chapter 339: Shock and Awe

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2003 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned seven.
She has said the year is defined by the invasion of {{p|Iraq}}.
A child of seven does not watch a war.
She watches the grown-ups watch it,
The green night of the cameras, the city lit by fire,
The word that the generals had chosen for the bombing,
Shock and awe, which children repeat
Because it sounds like something.
The war the speeches had built for a year
Was fought in the spring, and lost in the summer,
And went on long after the girl was grown.

## The shuttle

On Saturday the first of February the shuttle {{x|Columbia}}
Broke apart over {{p|Texas}} as it came home.
A piece of foam had struck its wing on the way up,
Sixteen days before, and the people who could have asked
Whether that mattered had decided it did not.
Seven died, among them {{c|Ilan Ramon}},
The first astronaut of {{p|Israel}},
And {{c|Kalpana Chawla}}, born in {{p|Karnal}} in {{p|India}}.
Pieces fell across two states.
The board that studied it later wrote
That the culture had learned to accept what it should have feared.

## The case

On the fifth of February {{c|Colin Powell}}
Spoke to the {{x|Security Council}} for more than an hour,
With photographs, recordings, and a small vial held up to the room,
And made the case that {{p|Iraq}} held weapons of mass destruction.
Much of it came from a single source, called {{x|Curveball}},
Whom the services that held him did not trust.
No such weapons were found.
{{c|Powell}} later called the speech a blot on his record.
A case is not a fact because the person making it is honorable.

## The largest protest

On the fifteenth of February, in some six hundred cities,
People marched against the war that had not yet begun.
In {{p|Rome}}, perhaps three million; in {{p|London}}, perhaps a million;
In {{p|Madrid}}, {{p|Barcelona}}, {{p|Berlin}}, {{p|Paris}}, {{p|New York}}, {{p|Melbourne}}.
It may have been the largest protest the world has seen.
The counts are not agreed, and this chapter does not choose.
The war began a month later.
A crowd can be the largest ever and still be told no.

## The invasion

On the twentieth of March the bombs fell on {{p|Baghdad}}.
The armies of the {{p|United States}} and {{p|Britain}}, with {{p|Australia}} and {{p|Poland}},
Crossed from {{p|Kuwait}}.
In three weeks they reached the capital.
On the ninth of April, in {{x|Firdos Square}},
A statue of {{c|Saddam Hussein}} was pulled down,
With an American armored vehicle doing most of the pulling,
And the cameras close enough to make the crowd look larger.
In those same days the national museum was looted,
And the soldiers guarding the oil ministry
Were not sent to guard the tablets and the vases
Of the oldest cities in this book.
Some of what was taken came back. Much did not.

On the first of May the president landed on an aircraft carrier
Under a banner that said mission accomplished,
And said the major combat was over.
Most of the dying of that war was still to come.

## The orders

In May the American administrator, {{c|Paul Bremer}},
Signed an order removing the members of the ruling party from their posts,
And another dissolving the army.
Hundreds of thousands of armed men with families
Were sent home without pay and without a future.
Many of them found the insurgency.
On the nineteenth of August a truck bomb destroyed
The headquarters of the {{x|United Nations}} in {{p|Baghdad}},
And killed {{c|Sérgio Vieira de Mello}}, its envoy, and twenty-one others.
The weapons were looked for all year.
The team that looked found none.
On the thirteenth of December {{c|Saddam Hussein}} was found
In a hole in the ground near {{p|Tikrit}},
Bearded, and he gave himself up.
His trial and his death are later chapters.

## The sickness

The cough that began in {{p|Foshan}} the November before
Spread in the spring.
A doctor who had treated it in {{p|Guangzhou}}
Stayed in a hotel in {{p|Hong Kong}} in February,
And guests from that hotel carried it to {{p|Toronto}}, {{p|Hanoi}}, {{p|Singapore}}.
{{c|Carlo Urbani}}, the doctor in {{p|Hanoi}} who first warned the world of it,
Caught it and died on the twenty-ninth of March.
The {{x|World Health Organization}} issued a global alert.
Some eight thousand fell ill and some seven hundred and seventy died.
By the summer it was contained,
By masks, by quarantine, by tracing,
And it did not come back.
The next one, in seventeen years, would not be contained.

## The finished letters

On Monday the fourteenth of April, in {{p|Bethesda}},
An international consortium announced
That the human genome had been sequenced, and called it finished,
More than two years before the schedule.
Finished meant fewer than one error in ten thousand letters,
And fewer than four hundred gaps
In the part that carries the genes.
{{c|Francis Collins}} said it was not completely complete,
And perhaps never would be.
{{c|Robert Waterston}} said: we have before us the instruction set
That carries each of us from the one-cell egg
Through adulthood to the grave.
The sentence is his.
A reference is not each life.
It was a map of the letters, not a reading of them,
And this book, which counts the lines of descent,
Knows the difference between a list of names and a story.

## The courts and the bodies

On the twenty-sixth of June, in {{x|Lawrence v. Texas}},
The {{x|Supreme Court}} of the {{p|United States}}
Struck down the laws that made love between two men a crime.
Two men had been arrested in their own bedroom in {{p|Houston}}.
On the eighteenth of November the high court of {{p|Massachusetts}}
Ruled that the state could not deny marriage
To two people of the same sex.
The first such marriages there are the next chapter.
These were the years the law began to turn,
And a child who would later turn too
Was growing up inside the turning, not knowing it was hers.

## The heat and the dark

On the fourteenth of August the power failed
Across the northeast of the continent,
From {{p|Ohio}} to {{p|New York}} to {{p|Ontario}},
Fifty-five million people,
Because a software alarm in one control room had stopped,
And trees had touched a line.
In {{p|Europe}} that summer a heat wave killed
Perhaps seventy thousand people,
Most of them old, many of them alone in apartments in {{p|Paris}}
While their families were away on holiday.
The heat was the first of the great heats of the century.
It was not the last, and it was not the worst.

## The rest of the year

In February the war in {{p|Darfur}} began,
And the government's horsemen burned the villages of the west.
In March {{c|Hu Jintao}} became president of {{p|China}}.
In August {{c|Charles Taylor}} left {{p|Liberia}}.
On the twenty-fourth of October the {{x|Concorde}} flew its last paying flight,
And the world got slower, on purpose.
On the fifteenth of October {{c|Yang Liwei}} went into orbit,
The first astronaut of {{p|China}}.
On the twenty-third of November, in {{p|Tbilisi}},
The {{x|Rose Revolution}} put out the old president of {{p|Georgia}},
With roses carried into the parliament.
That country will come back to this month, invaded, five chapters on.
In the summer {{x|MySpace}} opened, and {{x|Skype}},
And a world called {{x|Second Life}},
And people began to live some of their life in rooms with no walls.

## The year held

A shuttle fell, the largest crowd in history said no,
And a war was begun on a case that was not true.
A statue was pulled down for the cameras,
A museum was emptied while the oil was guarded,
An army was sent home with its guns.
A sickness was stopped, the letters of a genome were set down,
A court let two men love each other in their own house,
The lights went out, and the old died in the heat.
A girl of seven watched the grown-ups watch it.

Refuse the consolation that a war begun on a false case
Was begun in good faith because its makers believed it,
And the consolation that the crowd that said no
Was proved right by saying it.
It was proved right by the war.


# Chapter 340: A Friend of a Friend

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2004 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned eight.
She has said that 2004 is not the year Facebook started,
Meaning that the year is more than that, and so it is.
It was the year the companies that would hold her generation's attention
Were born or came of age,
The year the sea killed more people in a morning than any war that year,
And the year the war of the year before showed its photographs.
A child of eight is old enough to remember a wave on a screen,
And young enough to think it is far away.

## The book of faces

On Wednesday the fourth of February, in {{p|Cambridge}},
{{c|Mark Zuckerberg}}, a student, after about a week of coding,
Opened {{x|thefacebook.com}}.
The houses of the college already kept books of faces.
He said it was silly that the college would take years to make one,
And that he could do it better, and in a week.
A person with a {{p|Harvard}} address could put up a picture,
Their courses and their interests,
And search for a friend, or a friend of a friend.
In four days there were more than six hundred and fifty.
In two weeks, more than four thousand.
He said the nature of the site was that each person's experience
Improves if their friends join.
He said he would not sell anybody's e-mail address.
Within weeks it reached {{p|Columbia}}, {{p|Stanford}}, {{p|Yale}}.
That summer he moved to {{p|California}} with {{c|Dustin Moskovitz}}
And took half a million dollars from {{c|Peter Thiel}}.
The friend of a friend became the product,
And the product became the way a generation found itself and lost itself.
The girl was eight. It would reach her in time,
As it reached nearly everyone.

## The mail and the money

On the first of April {{x|Google}} offered a mail service
With hundreds of times the storage of the others,
And people thought the date meant it was a joke.
It was not. It read the mail to place the ads beside it.
On the nineteenth of August the company sold its stock to the public,
In an auction, at eighty-five dollars a share,
And its founders kept the votes.

In October, at the book fair in {{p|Frankfurt}},
{{c|Larry Page}} and {{c|Sergey Brin}} showed a search inside books,
The few pages around a phrase, and a link to a shop.
On the fourteenth of December the company said
It would scan the libraries of {{p|Harvard}}, {{p|Stanford}}, {{p|Michigan}},
{{p|Oxford}}, and the public library of {{p|New York}}.
{{c|Page}} said they had dreamed of making searchable
What librarians lovingly organize.
The authors and the publishers sued the next year.
A library scanned is not a library read,
And a company that holds the scan holds something new.

## The trains

On the eleventh of March, in {{p|Madrid}},
Ten bombs went off on four commuter trains in the morning rush.
One hundred and ninety-three people were killed.
The government blamed the Basque separatists,
Because an election was three days away.
It was men tied to the men of the planes.
The voters learned it before the vote,
And turned the government out.
The lie about the dead was the government's undoing.

## The photographs

On the twenty-eighth of April a television program in the {{p|United States}}
Showed photographs from {{x|Abu Ghraib}}, a prison near {{p|Baghdad}}:
Prisoners naked and stacked, a hooded man on a box with wires on his hands,
A prisoner on a leash, and the smiling soldiers beside them.
The pictures had been taken by the soldiers, for themselves.
The army called it the work of a few.
The memos that had loosened the rules on questioning
Came from much higher.
In {{p|Fallujah}} in March, four contractors were killed,
Their bodies burned and hung from a bridge.
The city was besieged twice that year,
And in November the second siege leveled much of it.

## The school

On the first of September, the first day of school, in {{p|Beslan}},
In {{p|North Ossetia}}, armed men from the war in {{p|Chechnya}}
Took more than eleven hundred people hostage in a school gymnasium,
Most of them children and their parents, there for the first-day ceremony.
They held them three days without water in the September heat.
On the third, bombs went off in the gym, and the soldiers stormed it.
Three hundred and thirty-four hostages died,
One hundred and eighty-six of them children.
A girl of eight in another country started a school year that week too.

## The union and the revolutions

On the first of May ten countries joined the {{x|European Union}},
Most of them from the old empire of the east:
{{p|Poland}}, {{p|Czechia}}, {{p|Slovakia}}, {{p|Hungary}}, {{p|Slovenia}},
{{p|Estonia}}, {{p|Latvia}}, {{p|Lithuania}}, {{p|Malta}}, {{p|Cyprus}}.
The wall had been down fifteen years.
In {{p|Ukraine}}, in the autumn, the candidate of the west,
{{c|Viktor Yushchenko}}, was poisoned with dioxin, and lived, scarred.
The vote of November was stolen,
And the people stood in the snow of the {{p|Maidan}} in orange for weeks
Until the court ordered the vote held again,
And he won the vote of December.
The country whose candidate lost that vote would invade, ten years later,
And this month will reach it.

## The marriages

In February the mayor of {{p|San Francisco}}, {{c|Gavin Newsom}},
Began marrying couples of the same sex, against the state's law,
And the line went around the block in the rain.
The courts voided those marriages.
On the seventeenth of May, in {{p|Massachusetts}},
Marriages of the same sex began under the court's ruling,
The first in the country that held.
On the second of November eleven states voted
To write a ban on them into their constitutions,
And the same day {{c|George W. Bush}} was elected to a second term,
And it was said the bans had brought out his voters.
The turning of the law was not a straight line.
It went forward in one state and back in eleven on the same year.

## The deaths

On the fifth of June {{c|Ronald Reagan}} died.
On the second of November, in {{p|Amsterdam}},
The filmmaker {{c|Theo van Gogh}} was shot and stabbed in the street
For a film about the treatment of women in {{x|Islam}},
And a letter was pinned to his body with the knife.
On the eleventh of November {{c|Yasser Arafat}} died, in a hospital near {{p|Paris}}.
In {{p|Haiti}} the elected president was flown out in February
And did not come back.
In September the American secretary of state
Called what was happening in {{p|Darfur}} a genocide.
Calling it that did not stop it.

## The sky

In January two rovers landed on {{p|Mars}}, {{x|Spirit}} and {{x|Opportunity}},
Built to last ninety days.
One worked for six years, the other for fourteen.
On the first of July {{x|Cassini}} reached {{p|Saturn}}.
On the fourth of October {{x|SpaceShipOne}}, built with private money,
Went to the edge of space for the second time in a week, and won a prize for it.
In August the games came home to {{p|Athens}}.

## The wave

On the twenty-sixth of December, the day after Christmas,
The sea floor off {{p|Sumatra}} broke along a thousand kilometers,
One of the largest earthquakes ever measured.
The wave crossed the {{x|Indian Ocean}} in hours,
And struck {{p|Indonesia}}, {{p|Sri Lanka}}, {{p|India}}, {{p|Thailand}},
And as far as {{p|Somalia}}.
In {{p|Aceh}} it went miles inland.
About two hundred and thirty thousand people died,
In a single morning, with no warning system in that ocean.
Tourists filmed the water going out, and walked toward it,
Because no one had told them what it meant.
The warning system was built afterward.
The girl was eight, on the second day of the holidays.
The world was on the screen, and it was water.

## The year held

A book of faces, a mail that read the mail, a company that scanned the libraries,
Bombs on the trains in {{p|Madrid}}, photographs from a prison,
A school in {{p|Beslan}}, ten countries joined, an orange square in {{p|Kyiv}},
Marriages begun in one state and banned in eleven,
Rovers on {{p|Mars}}, and a wave that killed a city's worth of people in an hour.

Refuse the consolation that the photographs were the work of a few,
And the consolation that a friend of a friend is a friend.
Refuse the consolation that the people who walked toward the water were fools.
They had not been told.


# Chapter 341: The Water and the Levees

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2005 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned nine.
The year had had no chapter of its own in this book until now,
Which says something about the book and nothing about the year.
It was the year a city drowned in the richest country in the world,
The year a pope died and another was chosen,
The year the moving pictures of anyone at all
Got a place to live,
And the year two countries opened marriage to everyone,
One of them the country she would grow up in.

## The pictures

On the fourteenth of February three young men who had worked at a payments company
Registered an address for sharing videos.
On the twenty-third of April one of them, {{c|Jawed Karim}},
Put up the first one: eighteen seconds of himself at the zoo in {{p|San Diego}},
Standing before the elephants,
Saying that the cool thing about them is that they have really, really, really long trunks.
That is the whole of it.
The site was called {{x|YouTube}}.
A year and a half later it was sold for more than a billion and a half dollars.
The children who were nine that year
Would grow up with a camera that could reach everyone,
And some of them would grow up on it.
In June two students opened a board of links called {{x|Reddit}},
And faked the early users to make it look full.
In February {{x|Google Maps}} put the streets of the world
Into a page that could be dragged with the hand.

## The pope

On the second of April {{c|John Paul II}} died in {{p|Rome}},
After twenty-six years, the first pope from {{p|Poland}},
Who had helped bring down the empire of the east,
And who would not move on women, or on the people the next popes would still not move on.
Millions came to his funeral.
On the nineteenth of April the cardinals chose {{c|Joseph Ratzinger}},
His enforcer of doctrine for twenty-four years,
Who took the name {{c|Benedict XVI}}.
He would do the rarest thing a pope can do,
And step down, eight years later, in this month.

## The trains and the bus

On the seventh of July, in {{p|London}}, in the morning rush,
Three bombs went off in the underground, and one on a bus at {{p|Tavistock Square}}.
Fifty-two people were killed.
The four bombers were young men, three of them born in {{p|Britain}}.
The day before, {{p|London}} had been given the games of 2012,
And the city had celebrated.

## The drowning

On the twenty-ninth of August the storm called {{x|Katrina}}
Came ashore near the border of {{p|Louisiana}} and {{p|Mississippi}}.
In {{p|New Orleans}} the levees the army's engineers had built
Failed in more than fifty places,
And four parts in five of the city went under water.
The people who could leave had left.
The people who could not, most of them poor, most of them black,
Were left in their attics, on their roofs,
In the stadium with no power and no water,
And at the convention center, where no one came for days.
About eighteen hundred people died.
The head of the federal agency for disasters
Had run an association of horse shows before.
The president told him he was doing a heck of a job.
The government knew where the water was.
It did not come.
A girl of nine, far to the north, saw the roofs on the screen
With words painted on them asking for help.

## The earthquake

On the eighth of October the earth broke under {{p|Kashmir}},
On both sides of the line between {{p|Pakistan}} and {{p|India}},
In the morning, while children were in their schools.
More than eighty thousand people died, many of them children,
Under the schools that were not built to stand.
Winter came to the mountains before the shelters did.

## The marriages

On the third of July {{p|Spain}}, a country of the old faith,
Opened marriage to two people of the same sex.
On the twentieth of July {{p|Canada}} did the same,
By a law of the whole country, the {{x|Civil Marriage Act}},
After the courts of most of its provinces had already said so.
{{p|Canada}} was the fourth country in the world to do it,
And the first in the Americas.
The girl of nine grew up in that country.
A law is made before the people who will need it know they will.
That is what such a law is for.

## The fingers and the cedars

On the thirtieth of January the people of {{p|Iraq}} voted,
And held up fingers stained purple with the ink,
While the bombs went off at the polling places.
In October they voted on a constitution,
And in December for a parliament.
The voting did not stop the war.
On the fourteenth of February, in {{p|Beirut}},
A bomb of a ton of explosives killed the former prime minister, {{c|Rafic Hariri}},
And the people of {{p|Lebanon}} filled the squares,
And the army of {{p|Syria}}, there for twenty-nine years, went home by April.
They called it the {{x|Cedar Revolution}}.
In August {{p|Israel}} pulled its settlers and soldiers out of {{p|Gaza}},
And {{p|Gaza}} was left to what came after.
On the thirteenth of May, in {{p|Andijan}}, in {{p|Uzbekistan}},
Soldiers fired on a crowd in the square, and killed hundreds.
The government said nearly two hundred, all of them terrorists.
On the twenty-eighth of July the {{x|IRA}} said it was done with the gun.

## The treaty and the cartoons

On the sixteenth of February the {{x|Kyoto Protocol}} came into force,
Binding the rich countries to cut their gases, a little,
Without the {{p|United States}}, which had walked away from it.
{{p|Canada}} signed it and later walked away too.
On the thirtieth of September a newspaper in {{p|Denmark}}
Printed twelve cartoons of the {{x|Prophet}},
To show that it could.
The answer came in the next year, in fire and in deaths,
And this book does not choose between the paper's right and the anger,
Except to say that both were real, and neither was the whole.

## The rest of the year

In January the probe {{x|Huygens}} landed on {{p|Titan}},
The farthest landing ever made,
And in the same month astronomers found a world beyond {{p|Pluto}}
Larger than it, which they later named {{x|Eris}},
And which would cost {{p|Pluto}} its place among the planets the year after.
In March {{c|Terri Schiavo}}, kept alive for fifteen years,
Was let to die after the courts and the congress fought over her body.
On the thirty-first of May the man called {{x|Deep Throat}}
Said that he was {{c|Mark Felt}}.
In June {{p|Iran}} elected {{c|Mahmoud Ahmadinejad}}.
On the second of July the concerts called {{x|Live 8}}
Asked the rich countries to forgive the debts of the poor.
On the twenty-fourth of October {{c|Rosa Parks}} died.
In October and November the suburbs of {{p|Paris}} burned,
After two boys died hiding from the police in a power station.
On the twenty-second of November {{c|Angela Merkel}} became chancellor of {{p|Germany}},
And held it for sixteen years.
In November an article in the open encyclopedia
Said falsely that a journalist, {{c|John Seigenthaler}},
Had been suspected in the killing of the {{c|Kennedy}}s.
It had stood four months.
He wrote that he had no way to know who had written it.
The open book tightened its rules a little.
The labor that kept it true was still unpaid.

## The year held

A video of elephants, a link board faking its first users, a map you drag.
A pope buried, a pope chosen, bombs in {{p|London}}, a city drowned.
A mountain fell on its schools.
Two countries opened marriage, and one of them was hers.
Purple fingers, cedars in the square, a massacre in {{p|Andijan}}, a treaty without its largest polluter,
Twelve cartoons, a world larger than {{p|Pluto}}, and the suburbs on fire.

Refuse the consolation that the water killed the people of {{p|New Orleans}}.
The water came, and the help did not.
Refuse the consolation that a law is too far away to matter to a child.
It is waiting for whoever needs it.


# Chapter 342: The Typed Name

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2006 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned ten.
Twenty years later she would spend her nights in the records
That strangers began to type this year,
Following her mothers and fathers back through the parishes of {{p|Sweden}}
And the farms of {{p|Germany}}, and further,
To the point where this book's own genealogy begins.
She did not know any of that at ten.
Nobody types a name for the child who will need it.
They type it anyway.

## The typed names

On Tuesday the first of August, in {{p|Provo}},
{{c|Marlin K. Jensen}}, the historian of the {{x|Latter-day Saints}},
Said the millions of rolls of film the church had kept,
In a vault cut into a mountain in {{p|Utah}},
Were being scanned,
And that a scanned record still had to be typed
Before a person could search it.
The typing was opened to volunteers,
Each record typed twice by two strangers,
And a third deciding when they differed.
By the next summer some fifty thousand were typing,
The marriages of {{p|Indiana}}, the census of nineteen hundred,
The parish books of countries none of them would visit.
The church's reason was its own:
The history ships and the temple receives,
And the dead were to be offered what the living had.
This book does not share that reason.
It shares the labor's result:
Free indexes, linked to the images,
Made by a community no one paid.
That is the same unpaid labor she would later hate in the encyclopedia.
The difference she would draw is whose it was, and what it was for,
And whether the ones who gave it were broken by the giving.
This chapter does not draw it for her.

## The small messages

On the twenty-first of March {{c|Jack Dorsey}}
Sent the first message on a service limited to a hundred and forty letters,
Just setting up my twttr.
It was called {{x|Twitter}}.
It would become the room where the century argued,
And later a room one man bought, and changed.
On the fifth of September the book of faces gave every user
A feed of what their friends were doing,
And the users protested, by the hundreds of thousands, on the feed.
On the twenty-sixth of September it opened to anyone over thirteen
With an e-mail address.
On the ninth of October {{x|Google}} bought the site of videos
For one billion six hundred and fifty million dollars.
In March {{x|Amazon}} began to rent its storage,
And in August its computers, by the hour,
And the companies of the next twenty years
Would be built on machines they never saw.
In December a magazine named its person of the year:
You, with a mirror on the cover.
The you was the unpaid user.

## The planet that was not

On the twenty-fourth of August, in {{p|Prague}},
The astronomers of the world voted on what a planet is,
And {{p|Pluto}} was not one.
A world larger than it had been found beyond it the year before,
And either both were planets or neither.
They chose neither.
Children who had learned nine learned eight.
A definition is a vote. The rock did not change.

## The war of the summer

On the twelfth of July {{x|Hezbollah}} crossed into {{p|Israel}},
Killed soldiers, and took two.
{{p|Israel}} bombed {{p|Lebanon}} for thirty-four days,
The airport, the bridges, the south of {{p|Beirut}},
And {{x|Hezbollah}} fired thousands of rockets into the north of {{p|Israel}}.
More than a thousand Lebanese died, most of them civilians,
And some hundred and sixty Israelis, most of them soldiers.
A ceasefire came in August.
Neither side said it had lost.

## The civil war

On the twenty-second of February, in {{p|Samarra}},
Bombs destroyed the golden dome of the {{x|al-Askari Shrine}},
Holy to the {{x|Shia}}.
In the months after, the killing between {{x|Shia}} and {{x|Sunni}} in {{p|Iraq}}
Became a civil war,
Bodies found each morning in {{p|Baghdad}} with their hands bound.
On the eighth of November, the day after his party lost the congress,
{{c|Donald Rumsfeld}}, who had run the war, resigned.
On the thirtieth of December {{c|Saddam Hussein}} was hanged,
At dawn, on the first day of the feast,
While the guards chanted the name of a rival,
And a phone filmed it,
And the film went everywhere.
A trial ended in a lynching's manners.

## The test and the poison

On the ninth of October {{p|North Korea}} tested its first nuclear weapon,
Underground, small, and real.
On the seventh of October, in {{p|Moscow}}, {{c|Anna Politkovskaya}},
Who had written of the war in {{p|Chechnya}},
Was shot in the elevator of her building, on the birthday of the president.
On the first of November, in a hotel in {{p|London}},
{{c|Alexander Litvinenko}}, who had fled the Russian service,
Drank tea with two men from it,
And the tea held {{x|polonium}}, a metal that burns from the inside.
He died on the twenty-third, and named the man he said had ordered it.
An inquiry later named the same man.

## The votes

On the twenty-fifth of January {{x|Hamas}} won the elections in {{p|Palestine}},
And the countries that had asked for the elections
Cut off the money because of who had won.
On the sixth of February {{c|Stephen Harper}} became prime minister of {{p|Canada}},
The country she grew up in,
And held it nine years.
On the sixteenth of January {{c|Ellen Johnson Sirleaf}} became president of {{p|Liberia}},
The first woman elected to lead a country in {{p|Africa}}.
On the twenty-second {{c|Evo Morales}} became president of {{p|Bolivia}},
The first from its indigenous majority.
On the third of June {{p|Montenegro}} became a country.
On the nineteenth of September the army of {{p|Thailand}} took the government.

## The rest of the year

On the eleventh of July bombs on the commuter trains of {{p|Mumbai}}
Killed two hundred and nine people.
In May a former vice president, {{c|Al Gore}}, put his slides of the warming world into a film,
{{x|An Inconvenient Truth}}, and people went to see a lecture in a cinema.
In the winter the new game machines came out,
And one of them, the {{x|Wii}}, was waved with the hand,
And grandparents bowled in their living rooms.

## The year held

A girl of ten, and twenty years ahead of her, a night in the typed records.
The first strangers typing the names of the dead, twice, for nothing.
A hundred and forty letters, a feed of friends, the videos sold,
A planet voted out, a summer war, a civil war, a hanging filmed on a phone,
A bomb tested underground, a writer shot in an elevator, poison in the tea,
Votes the voters' patrons would not accept, and a lecture that filled the cinemas.

Refuse the consolation that free labor is free.
Someone pays, and it is not the one who takes it.
Refuse the consolation that the name typed for no one was typed for no one.


# Chapter 343: One Device

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2007 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned eleven.
It was the year the phone became the window,
The year a spit in a tube by mail would tell you where your blood had been,
And the year the money of the world began to fail
While the people in charge said it was contained.
A child of eleven feels a year like that in the house before she reads it in a paper.
What she felt of it is hers and is not written here.

## The device

On Tuesday the ninth of January, in {{p|San Francisco}},
{{c|Steve Jobs}} showed a phone that was not yet for sale.
He said he was introducing three products:
A wide music player, with the glass as its control,
A phone,
And a machine for the net.
Then he said they were not three. They were one device.
He called it the {{x|iPhone}}.
It went on sale on the twenty-ninth of June,
And people stood in line for days.
In September he cut the price by two hundred dollars,
And the people who had stood in line were angry,
And he gave them a credit at the store.
In November the company that owned the search
Announced {{x|Android}}, an open system for the phones of everyone else.
By the time the girl of eleven was grown
Nearly everyone on earth would carry one device,
And the century would be lived through a pane of glass,
Including this book, which most will read on one.

## The spit by mail

On Monday the nineteenth of November, in {{p|Mountain View}},
{{c|Anne Wojcicki}} and {{c|Linda Avey}} began selling a test of the blood by mail.
You spat in a tube and sent it,
And for nine hundred and ninety-nine dollars
Some half a million places on your chromosomes were read,
Telling you of disease, of traits, and of ancestry.
The company was {{x|23andMe}}.
Ancestry is not the whole of the reading.
Disease is not a descent.
A count of markers is not the whole sequence.
Millions would send their spit in the years after,
And give the company their bodies' letters,
And the company would later fail, and its letters be sold.
This book traces descent by records and by joining them.
The blood tells a different story, and the two are not one.

## The money

In February the lenders who had sold houses to people
Who could not pay for them began to fail.
In April the largest of them, {{x|New Century}}, went bankrupt.
On the ninth of August the bank {{x|BNP Paribas}}, in {{p|Paris}},
Froze three of its funds, saying it could no longer value what was in them,
And the banks of the world stopped lending to each other overnight.
On the fourteenth of September people stood in line outside the bank
{{x|Northern Rock}}, in {{p|England}}, to take their money out,
The first such run on a British bank in more than a century.
The men in charge said it was contained.
It was the next year's chapter, and it was not contained.

## The shootings and the bridge

On the sixteenth of April, at {{x|Virginia Tech}},
A student killed thirty-two people and then himself,
The worst such killing the country had seen up to then.
It would not stay the worst.
On the first of August a bridge carrying the interstate
Across the {{x|Mississippi}} in {{p|Minneapolis}}
Fell into the river at the evening rush.
Thirteen died.
A gusset plate had been too thin since it was built.

## The surge and the war

On the tenth of January {{c|George W. Bush}} sent more than twenty thousand more soldiers to {{p|Iraq}},
And called it a surge.
The killing fell by the end of the year.
Whether the surge caused it, or the {{x|Sunni}} tribes turning against the jihadists,
Or the cleansing of {{p|Baghdad}}'s neighborhoods already done,
Is argued still.
In September, in {{p|Myanmar}}, the monks marched in their saffron robes
Against the generals, and the generals shot them.

## The assassination

On the twenty-seventh of December, in {{p|Rawalpindi}},
{{c|Benazir Bhutto}}, who had come home to {{p|Pakistan}} in October to run for office again,
And whose homecoming had been bombed, killing more than a hundred and fifty,
Was killed at a rally, by a gun and a bomb.
The same day, in {{p|Kenya}}, an election was held,
And the result announced three days later
Was fought over with machetes,
