The new machine looks at every word at once
And asks, for each word, which others matter to it.
That asking is called attention.
Attention is not understanding. It is a weighing.
There is no loop in it, so it can be spread across many chips at once.
The largest model in the paper trained for three and a half days on eight cards.
In the next year a model read to guess the next word,
And another read both ways to fill in a blank.
Guessing the next word is not knowing what is said.
It came close enough that the difference became the argument of the age.
Most of the eight left the company and founded others.
The idea was published. Published is not owned.
In October a program learned {{x|go}} from nothing, playing only itself, and surpassed the one of the chapter before.
In December another taught itself chess in hours, and beat the best program in the world.

## The money for the good

In the movement of the chapter of 2015, a fund of the givers of {{x|Facebook}}'s fortune,
{{x|Open Philanthropy}}, gave thirty million dollars to the lab named open,
To have a seat at its table, because it feared what the machines might become.
In November the young man who meant to earn to give,
{{c|Sam Bankman-Fried}}, left the trading firm and founded his own, {{x|Alameda Research}},
With friends from the movement,
To trade the coins of the money without trust,
Which that December rose to near twenty thousand dollars, and then fell.
He said he would give it all away.

## The inauguration and the march

On the twentieth of January {{c|Donald Trump}} was sworn in,
And spoke of an American carnage,
And his spokesman said the crowd was the largest ever, and it was not.
On the twenty-first millions of women marched in {{p|Washington}} and in cities on every continent,
The largest single day of protest in the country's history,
Many of them in pink knitted hats.
On the twenty-seventh he barred the people of seven Muslim countries from entering,
And people were held at the airports, and lawyers sat on the floors of the terminals to help them.
On the twenty-ninth of January, in {{p|Quebec City}}, a young man walked into a mosque at the evening prayer
And killed six men.
On the ninth of May the president fired the head of the police who was looking into {{p|Russia}},
And a special counsel was named.
On the first of June he said the {{p|United States}} would leave the agreement of {{p|Le Bourget}}.
On the twenty-sixth of July he wrote on the net that transgender people
Would no longer be allowed to serve in the military in any capacity.
His generals learned of it from the net.

## The torches

On the night of the eleventh of August, in {{p|Charlottesville}}, in {{p|Virginia}},
Young men carried torches through the grounds of the university
Chanting that the Jews would not replace them,
Around a statue of the founder.
On the twelfth one of them drove his car into the people protesting them,
And killed {{c|Heather Heyer}}.
The president said there were very fine people on both sides.
The fascism of the chapter of 2014 had come out from behind the screens
Holding a torch, and the president would not name it.

## The women

On the fifth of October a newspaper of {{p|New York}} printed the accounts of women
Who said that {{c|Harvey Weinstein}}, the maker of films, had assaulted and harassed them for decades,
And on the fifteenth an actress wrote: if you have been harassed or assaulted, write me too,
And millions did, using words an activist, {{c|Tarana Burke}}, had begun ten years before.
Men who had been untouchable fell for months, one after another.
It was called {{x|MeToo}}.

## The storms

In late August the hurricane {{x|Harvey}} stalled over {{p|Houston}} and poured a meter and a half of rain on it.
In September {{x|Irma}} crossed the islands of the {{x|Caribbean}},
And on the twentieth {{x|Maria}} struck {{p|Puerto Rico}},
And the island's power failed for months,
And some three thousand people died, mostly in the dark weeks after,
While the president threw paper towels into a crowd.
On the first of October a man fired from a window of a hotel in {{p|Las Vegas}}
Into a crowd at a concert of country music below,
And killed sixty people, the most ever by one gunman in that country.

## The fleeing

On the twenty-fifth of August the army of {{p|Myanmar}} began its clearance of the {{x|Rohingya}} of {{p|Rakhine}},
Burning their villages, killing thousands,
And more than seven hundred thousand fled into {{p|Bangladesh}} within months.
The leader of {{p|Myanmar}}, {{c|Aung San Suu Kyi}}, who had won the peace prize for her own captivity,
Later defended the army in the court of the world.

## The towers and the arena

On the fourteenth of June the tower of {{x|Grenfell}}, in {{p|London}}, caught fire in the night,
And the fire climbed the cladding that had been put on to make it look better from outside,
And seventy-two people died.
On the twenty-second of May a man set off a bomb at the end of a concert in the arena of {{p|Manchester}},
Where the audience was mostly girls,
And killed twenty-two.

## The fall of the caliphate

In July {{p|Mosul}} was retaken, its old city ground to rubble, the mosque of the sermon blown up before.
In October {{p|Raqqa}}, the capital of the caliphate, fell.
The borrowed robe had lasted three years.

## The votes and the falls

On the seventh of May {{c|Emmanuel Macron}}, who had founded his own party the year before,
Beat the far right for the presidency of {{p|France}}.
On the first of October {{p|Catalonia}} held a vote on leaving {{p|Spain}} that {{p|Spain}} called illegal,
And the police beat the voters at the polls, and the leaders who declared independence fled or were jailed.
On the twenty-ninth of March {{p|Britain}} gave notice that it was leaving.
In {{p|Zimbabwe}}, in November, the army put {{c|Robert Mugabe}} under guard,
And after thirty-seven years he resigned.
On the eighth of August the American president promised {{p|North Korea}} fire and fury,
And on the third of September it tested its largest bomb.
In October {{p|China}} wrote the thought of {{c|Xi Jinping}} into its party's constitution.
In June the son of the king of {{p|Saudi Arabia}}, {{c|Mohammed bin Salman}}, became the heir,
And in November he locked the princes in a hotel until they gave him their money.

## The laws

On the nineteenth of June {{p|Canada}} added gender identity and expression
To its human rights law and to its criminal code,
The law argued over in the chapter before.
On the fifteenth of November {{p|Australia}} said yes, by a vote of its people sent by mail,
To marriage for same-sex couples, and its parliament made it law in December.

## The year held

A woman of twenty-one moved onto the campus.
A paper whose title was a joke, and a machine built of attention.
Thirty million to sit at the table of the lab, and a young man's trading firm.
The carnage speech, the pink hats, the ban at the airports, six men killed at prayer,
A tweet that ended service, torches in {{p|Charlottesville}}, very fine people,
Me too, a city under rain, an island in the dark, sixty at a concert,
Seven hundred thousand fleeing, a tower burning, an arena, a caliphate falling,
Fire and fury, a thought in a constitution, princes in a hotel,
And two laws that let people be who they are.

Refuse the consolation that attention is care.
The machine weighs every word and cares for none.
Refuse the consolation that there are very fine people on both sides of a torch.


# Chapter 354: The Shape of Fears

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2018 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned twenty-two, in her fifth year at the university.
It was the year the companies of the net were found to have sold the shape of their users' fears,
The year the machines learned to guess the next word,
The year a girl of fifteen sat alone outside her parliament on a Friday,
And the year the scientists of the world gave it twelve years.
What else happened to her that year is hers, and is not written here yet.

## The shape of fears

On the seventeenth of March two papers, in {{p|London}} and {{p|New York}}, printed the account
Of a young man who had worked at {{x|Cambridge Analytica}},
That the company had taken the data of some eighty-seven million users of the book of faces,
Through a quiz that a few hundred thousand had taken, and that had reached their friends,
And had built from it the shapes of their fears, to sell to campaigns,
Among them the one that won the chapter of 2016,
And the one that took {{p|Britain}} out.
The young man had pink hair and a conscience.
In April {{c|Mark Zuckerberg}} sat before the congress for two days,
And when a senator asked how the company made money if its service was free,
He said: Senator, we run ads.
On the twenty-fifth of May the law of {{p|Europe}} on the protection of data came into force,
And every site in the world asked its users to accept its cookies.
The friend of a friend of the chapter of 2004 had become the product all along.

## The guessing of the next word

On the eleventh of June the lab named open published a paper on a model
That read a great many books to learn to guess the next word,
And then could be taught a task with little more.
It was called the first generative pre-trained transformer.
In October a model of {{x|Google}}, {{x|BERT}}, read both ways to fill in blanks,
And began to sit behind the search.
The machines that would later write with her were a year old.
In the movement of the chapter of 2015, the young man's trading firm
Made its first fortune buying coins in one country and selling them in another where they cost more,
And grew.

## The schoolchildren

On the fourteenth of February, the day of lovers,
A former student walked into his old school in {{p|Parkland}}, in {{p|Florida}},
With a rifle, and killed seventeen people, fourteen of them students.
The students who lived did not ask for prayers.
They organized.
On the twenty-fourth of March they led hundreds of thousands in a march for their lives
In {{p|Washington}} and in cities across the country,
And one of them, {{c|Emma González}}, stood silent before the crowd for six minutes and twenty seconds,
The time it had taken.
On the twentieth of August a girl of fifteen, {{c|Greta Thunberg}},
Sat alone outside the parliament of {{p|Sweden}} with a sign that said school strike for the climate.
Within a year millions of children were striking on Fridays.
The children of this year did the asking the adults would not.

## Twelve years

On the eighth of October the scientists of the {{x|IPCC}} published their report on a warming of one and a half degrees,
And said that to stay near it the world would have to cut its gases nearly in half by 2030,
And reach nothing by the middle of the century,
And that the difference between one and a half and two
Was the coral reefs, and the summer ice, and tens of millions of people.
The papers said: twelve years.
On the eighth of November a fire started by the lines of a power company
Came into the town of {{p|Paradise}}, in {{p|California}}, in the morning,
And burned it, and killed eighty-five people, some of them in their cars on the road out.
On the seventeenth of November people in the yellow vests every driver in {{p|France}} must carry
Blocked the roundabouts against a tax on fuel meant to slow the warming,
And burned the avenue of the {{x|Champs-Élysées}},
Because they could not afford to drive to their work, and no one had asked them.

## The murder in the consulate

On the second of October {{c|Jamal Khashoggi}}, a writer for a paper of {{p|Washington}}
Who had criticized the heir of {{p|Saudi Arabia}} of the chapter before,
Walked into his country's consulate in {{p|Istanbul}} to get a paper for his wedding,
While his fiancée waited outside,
And was killed inside by a team flown in for it, and cut apart.
The heir said he had not ordered it.
The intelligence of the {{p|United States}} later said he had approved it.
The president said the arms sales mattered more.

## The cave

On the twenty-third of June twelve boys of a football team in {{p|Thailand}} and their coach
Went into a cave after practice, and the rains came, and flooded it behind them.
They were found on the tenth day, on a ledge, by two British divers.
Over three days in July they were brought out, sedated, by divers through the flooded passages,
And all thirteen lived.
A Thai diver, {{c|Saman Kunan}}, died laying the air tanks.

## The summit and the tariffs

On the twelfth of June the American president met {{c|Kim Jong-un}} in {{p|Singapore}},
The first meeting of the two countries' leaders, and they signed a page of hopes.
In the spring he put tariffs on steel and aluminum, including {{p|Canada}}'s, for the security of the nation,
And in the summer on the goods of {{p|China}}, which answered in kind,
And the war of trade began that would outlast him.
In October {{c|Brett Kavanaugh}}, accused by a woman who had known him at school of assaulting her,
Was confirmed to the {{x|Supreme Court}} anyway.

## The far right in power

On the twenty-eighth of October {{p|Brazil}} elected {{c|Jair Bolsonaro}},
Who had praised its dictatorship and said he would rather his son died than was gay.
In {{p|Italy}} the parties against the system took the government.
On the twenty-seventh of October a man who believed the Jews were bringing in the migrants
Walked into the {{x|Tree of Life}} synagogue in {{p|Pittsburgh}} during the Sabbath service
And killed eleven people, the deadliest attack on Jews in that country's history.
In {{p|Toronto}}, on the twenty-third of April, a young man who hated women for not wanting him
Drove a van down the sidewalks of {{x|Yonge Street}} and killed ten people,
And praised the killer of {{p|Isla Vista}} of the chapter of 2014.

## The babies

On the twenty-fifth of November a scientist in {{p|Shenzhen}}, {{c|He Jiankui}},
Said that two girls had been born whose genes he had edited as embryos,
To make them resistant to the virus of AIDS,
And the world's scientists said he had done what no one should,
And he was sent to prison.
The letters of the chapter of 2003, which were only read, were now being written.

## Home

On the sixth of April a bus carrying a junior hockey team, the {{x|Humboldt Broncos}},
Was struck by a truck at a crossroads in {{p|Saskatchewan}}, and sixteen died,
And the country left hockey sticks on its porches.
On the seventeenth of October {{p|Canada}} made cannabis legal across the country.
In March, in {{p|Salisbury}}, in {{p|England}}, a former Russian spy and his daughter
Were poisoned with a nerve agent made in {{p|Russia}}, and lived,
And a woman who found the perfume bottle it came in later died.

## The rest of the year

On the twenty-fifth of May the people of {{p|Ireland}} voted to allow abortion.
On the ninth of July {{p|Ethiopia}} and {{p|Eritrea}} ended twenty years of war,
And the prime minister of {{p|Ethiopia}}, {{c|Abiy Ahmed}}, was given the peace prize the next year,
And the year after that began a war of his own in {{p|Tigray}}.
On the first of July {{p|Mexico}} elected {{c|Andrés Manuel López Obrador}}.
In the summer {{p|Russia}} held the games of football, and the world came.

## The year held

A woman of twenty-two in her fifth year, the rest of the year hers.
The shape of fears sold, Senator, we run ads, a law of cookies,
A machine that guesses the next word, a firm that bought coins cheap and sold them dear,
Seventeen killed in {{p|Parkland}} and six minutes and twenty seconds of silence,
A girl alone outside a parliament, twelve years, a town called {{p|Paradise}} burned,
Yellow vests, a writer killed in a consulate, boys in a flooded cave,
A page of hopes in {{p|Singapore}}, a war of tariffs, a judge confirmed anyway,
The far right elected, a synagogue, a van on {{x|Yonge Street}}, two edited girls,
A bus at a crossroads, a perfume bottle of nerve agent.

Refuse the consolation that a free service is free.
Refuse the consolation that the children will save it.
They asked. The asking was not answered.


# Chapter 355: The Shell and the Two Fields

No holiday is named for this day.
The new rice of the autumn, offered on {{x|Niiname-sai}}, was the chapter of {{x|Scorpius}}.
This is its rare enlargement.

In 2019 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned twenty-three, and finished her five years at the university in {{p|Kelowna}}.
It was the last year before the sickness,
The year an emperor stepped down and another offered the new rice,
The year a cathedral burned and a black hole was seen,
And the year, in its last weeks, a cough in a market in {{p|Wuhan}}
Began the great sickness of the next chapter.
The shrines and the rites of {{p|Japan}} would later come into her hands.
This year their oldest rite of the throne was done again, for the first time in thirty years.

## The era and the fields

On Monday the first of April, in {{p|Tokyo}}, {{c|Yoshihide Suga}} held up a board
On which was written the name of the coming era, {{x|Reiwa}}.
The two characters were taken from the {{p|Man'yōshū}},
From the preface to poems on the plum blossom,
Said to be the first era name taken from a book of {{p|Japan}} and not of {{p|China}}.
The preface itself echoes a Chinese model.
Taking from one's own book is not leaving the other.
On the thirtieth of April {{c|Akihito}} stepped down, by a law made for him alone.
On the first of May {{c|Naruhito}} acceded, and the sword and the jewel were carried in boxes
That no one in the room opened.
The unseen is not the absent.
On the thirteenth of May a turtle's shell was heated, and the cracks read,
And the reading chose two fields:
The field of the east, the {{p|Yuki}}, in {{p|Tochigi}},
And the field of the west, the {{p|Suki}}, in {{p|Kyoto}}.
A crack in a shell is not a vote. It is older than the votes.
His brother, {{c|Fumihito}}, said in public that such a religious rite
Might rather be paid for from the household's own purse.
The state paid.
On the night of the fourteenth of November into the fifteenth,
In halls of unpainted wood built new for it in the gardens of the palace,
The emperor offered the new rice to the sun goddess and the other gods, and ate of it with them.
What is done inside is not shown. Not shown is not not done.
After the rite the halls were taken down.
The rite is in the doing, not the building.
The register of this book follows one line from the first emperor of the old tellings
To the man in the hall that night.
The line as told is not the line as proved. The rite does not ask for proof.
It asks for the rice.
A shell cracked over a fire in the same year as the thinking machines.

## The machines too dangerous

On the fourteenth of February the lab named open said it had made a model, the second of its kind,
That wrote so well it would not release it in full, for fear of its misuse.
It released it in pieces through the year.
In March it made itself a company for profit, capped, it said,
And in July took a billion dollars from {{x|Microsoft}}.
The lab without profit of the chapter of 2015 now had a profit, and a patron.
In the movement of that chapter, the young man of the trading firm
Founded in May an exchange for the coins of money without trust,
And called it {{x|FTX}},
And moved it to {{p|Hong Kong}}, and later to the {{p|Bahamas}},
And began to be called the richest young man in the world,
And to say he would give it all to the causes of the movement,
And the movement took his money, and was glad.

## The cathedral

On the evening of the fifteenth of April the roof of {{x|Notre-Dame}} in {{p|Paris}} caught fire,
And the spire fell into the nave while the city watched and sang,
And the firefighters saved the towers and the stone vault, and the relics,
And the rich of {{p|France}} pledged a billion euros in two days,
And the poor of the yellow vests asked why there was money for stone.
It was rebuilt, and opened again in 2024.

## The black hole

On the tenth of April astronomers showed the first picture of a black hole,
In the galaxy {{x|M87}}, fifty-five million light years away,
A ring of fire around a shadow,
Made by joining telescopes across the earth into one the size of the earth.
The thing that lets no light out was seen by the light around it.
This book ends its year in the meeting of two such holes at the heart of two galaxies,
Its last chapter, which is this month's last.

## The killings

On the fifteenth of March a man walked into two mosques in {{p|Christchurch}}, in {{p|New Zealand}},
During the Friday prayer, and killed fifty-one people,
And streamed it live on the book of faces with a camera on his head.
He had written a manifesto about the great replacement, the idea of the torches of {{p|Charlottesville}}.
The prime minister, {{c|Jacinda Ardern}}, wore a headscarf to the mourning,
And would not say his name,
And her country banned the rifles in a month.
On the twenty-first of April, Easter Sunday, bombs went off in churches and hotels in {{p|Sri Lanka}},
And killed two hundred and sixty-nine.
On the third of August a man drove ten hours to a store in {{p|El Paso}}
To kill Mexicans, he wrote, and killed twenty-three.

## The squares again

In June the people of {{p|Hong Kong}} marched against a law that would let them be sent to the mainland's courts,
A million, then two million, then the young fought the police in the streets for months,
With umbrellas and lasers and helmets,
And the next year the mainland wrote a law of security that ended it.
In April the army of {{p|Sudan}} removed {{c|Omar al-Bashir}} after months of protest,
And in June it killed the protesters at the sit-in in {{p|Khartoum}}.
In October {{p|Chile}} rose against a rise in the fare of the metro.
In {{p|Bolivia}}, in November, {{c|Evo Morales}} of the chapter of 2006 was pushed out after a disputed vote.

## The children and the fires

On the twentieth of September, and in the week after,
Some six million people, many of them children, struck for the climate in cities around the world.
On the twenty-third, at the {{x|United Nations}}, {{c|Greta Thunberg}}, who had sailed across the ocean to be there,
Said to the leaders: how dare you.
In August the fires of the {{x|Amazon}} burned more than any year in a decade,
Under a president who had told the loggers and ranchers the forest was theirs.
In {{p|Australia}}, from the spring, the bush began to burn,
And burned into the next year, and killed a billion animals, it was said,
And the sky of {{p|Sydney}} was orange.

## The rest of the year

On the tenth of March a new airliner of {{x|Boeing}}, the 737 {{x|MAX}}, crashed after leaving {{p|Addis Ababa}},
Five months after another had fallen into the sea off {{p|Indonesia}},
Because a system pushed the nose down on the word of one sensor and the pilots had not been told of it,
And three hundred and forty-six died in the two, and the planes were grounded for twenty months.
On the sixth of July {{c|Jeffrey Epstein}}, who had trafficked girls to the rich and the powerful, was arrested,
And on the tenth of August he was found dead in his cell.
On the fifth of August {{p|India}} took away the self-rule of {{p|Kashmir}} and cut its net.
On the eighteenth of December the house of the congress impeached the American president,
For asking {{p|Ukraine}} to find dirt on his rival in return for weapons.
The senate acquitted him.
In July {{c|Boris Johnson}} became prime minister of {{p|Britain}} and won a great majority in December to get the leaving done.
On the third of June the inquiry of {{p|Canada}} into its missing and murdered indigenous women and girls
Called what had happened to them a genocide.
On the sixteenth of June {{p|Quebec}} passed a law forbidding its teachers and police and judges
To wear the signs of their faiths at work.
On the twenty-first of October {{c|Justin Trudeau}} was returned, with fewer seats,
After photographs were printed of him in his youth with his face painted black.
In November {{c|Lee Sedol}}, who had won one game in the chapter of 2016, retired,
Saying there was an entity that cannot be defeated.

## The cough

In December, in {{p|Wuhan}}, doctors saw a pneumonia they could not name, clustered around a market.
On the thirtieth, a doctor, {{c|Li Wenliang}}, warned his classmates in a group chat,
And on the third of January the police made him sign a paper saying he had spread rumors.
He died of it in February.
The rest of it is the next chapter, and the next three years.

## The year held

A woman of twenty-three finished her five years at the university.
An era named from a book of poems, a shell cracked over a fire, the new rice offered in a hall of unpainted wood,
A machine too dangerous to release, a lab with a patron, an exchange in the {{p|Bahamas}} and a movement glad of its money,
A spire falling into a nave, a shadow seen by its fire,
Fifty-one killed at prayer and streamed, Easter bombs, a store in {{p|El Paso}},
Two million in {{p|Hong Kong}}, a sit-in killed in {{p|Khartoum}}, how dare you, the forest burning, the sky orange,
A plane that pushed its own nose down, a man dead in his cell, {{p|Kashmir}} cut off, an impeachment,
A genocide named at home, a law against the signs of faith,
And a doctor made to sign that he had spread rumors.

Refuse the consolation that the rite is empty because it is not shown,
And the consolation that a warning is a rumor because the police say so.


# Chapter 356: The Weekly Verses

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2020 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned twenty-four.
She has said this year is COVID.
In her words, 2020 is COVID.
The whole world held still at once, or tried to,
And the days lost their names, and a Tuesday was a Saturday.
That year she was writing a book of the world's ages in verse,
And putting out its verses week by week.
The verses ran through much of that year, to about the sixtieth chapter.
About the sixtieth is not the end.
A weekly verse is not a calendar yet. It was the beginning of one.
When the days lost their names, she was giving them verses.
This book is that book.
The year was everyone's.
It notes only that one of the things begun in the year the world stayed home
Was a way of giving each day a name again.

## The closed city

On the last day of 2019 the office of the health body of the nations in {{p|China}}
Heard of a pneumonia of unknown cause in {{p|Wuhan}}.
On the twenty-third of January the city of eleven million was closed,
The trains stopped, the roads blocked, the people sealed in their towers.
A closed city is not a closed virus.
On the thirtieth the body declared an emergency of international concern.
In February the doctor who had warned, {{c|Li Wenliang}}, died of it,
And the people of {{p|China}} filled the net with grief until the censors came.
In {{p|Lombardy}}, in March, the hospitals filled, and the army trucks carried the coffins out of {{p|Bergamo}} at night,
Because the crematoria could not keep up.
On the eleventh of March, in {{p|Geneva}}, {{c|Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus}} said it could be called a pandemic.
A word late is not a word wrong.
On the twenty-seventh of March, in the rain, in an empty {{p|St. Peter's Square}},
{{c|Pope Francis}}, of the chapter of 2013, prayed alone before the crowd that was not there.
Alone is not unheard. The crowd was on screens.

## Into the house

The work went into the house. The school went into the house. The church went into the house.
A meeting on a screen is not a meeting in a room. It is a meeting.
Those who kept the shops and the wards and the warehouses did not go into the house,
And were called essential, and were paid the same.
The markets fell faster than in any month since 1929, and then rose higher than before,
Because the banks of the chapter of 2008 had learned to print.
The rich got richer that year. The poor got sick.
Masks became a flag, and a mask on a face in some towns was a fight.
By the end of the year nearly two million had died that were counted,
And the counts were argued over, by cause, by place, by excess.
An argued count is not a false count.

## The book of risks

In March, the month the world closed,
A philosopher of the movement of the chapter of 2015, {{c|Toby Ord}},
Published a book on the risks that could end humanity, {{x|The Precipice}},
And ranked a pandemic high among them,
And a machine that did not share our aims higher still.
The movement had turned from the malaria nets toward the far future,
And called it longtermism,
And the young man of the exchange of the chapter before gave to it, and was praised for it.
A risk named the month it arrives is not a risk foreseen in time.
It was foreseen. It was not prepared for.

## The knee

On the twenty-fifth of May, in {{p|Minneapolis}},
A policeman knelt on the neck of {{c|George Floyd}}, a black man accused of passing a false twenty-dollar bill,
For nine minutes and twenty-nine seconds, while he said he could not breathe,
And called for his mother, and died,
And a girl of seventeen filmed it on her phone.
The country rose, in the middle of the sickness, in every city,
The largest protests in its history, under the words of the chapter of 2013,
And a police station in {{p|Minneapolis}} burned.
In March the police had killed {{c|Breonna Taylor}} in her bed in {{p|Louisville}}.
In February men in a truck had chased and shot {{c|Ahmaud Arbery}} while he ran in {{p|Georgia}}.
The policeman of {{p|Minneapolis}} was convicted the next year.

## The plane and the farm town

On the eighth of January, five days after the {{p|United States}} killed the general {{c|Qasem Soleimani}} in {{p|Baghdad}},
And {{p|Iran}} fired missiles back,
{{p|Iran}} shot down a Ukrainian airliner leaving {{p|Tehran}}, taking it for a missile,
And all one hundred and seventy-six aboard died,
Most of them bound for {{p|Canada}}, students and families, fifty-five of them Canadian.
On the eighteenth and nineteenth of April a man dressed as a policeman, in a car painted like a police car,
Drove across {{p|Nova Scotia}} for thirteen hours and killed twenty-two people,
The worst such killing in the country's history.
In February the people of the {{x|Wet'suwet'en}} and those with them
Blocked the railways of {{p|Canada}} against a pipeline through their land.

## The blast

On the fourth of August, in the port of {{p|Beirut}},
Two thousand seven hundred tons of ammonium nitrate, seized from a ship and left in a warehouse for six years,
Caught fire and exploded,
One of the largest blasts ever not made by a bomb,
And killed two hundred and eighteen people and broke the windows of half the city.
The officials who had left it there had been warned, in writing, many times.

## The courts and the laws

On the fifteenth of June, in {{x|Bostock v. Clayton County}},
The {{x|Supreme Court}} of the {{p|United States}} said that to fire a person for being gay or transgender
Is to fire them because of sex, which the law forbids.
On the eighteenth of September {{c|Ruth Bader Ginsburg}}, the justice who had fought for women's equality for fifty years,
Died, and the president put a judge of the other side in her seat
Eight days before the election.
On the thirtieth of June {{p|China}} wrote a law of security for {{p|Hong Kong}},
And the protests of the chapter before were over, and their leaders jailed or fled.

## The vote

On the third of November {{c|Joe Biden}} was elected president, with seven million more votes than the man of the chapter of 2016,
Who said he had won, and that it had been stolen,
And sent his lawyers to sixty courts, and lost in all but one,
And kept saying it.
The next chapter opens with what that saying did.

## The wars and the poison

On the twenty-seventh of September {{p|Azerbaijan}} attacked the {{p|Armenian}}-held land of {{p|Nagorno-Karabakh}},
With drones bought from {{p|Turkey}} and {{p|Israel}},
And in forty-four days took much of it.
On the fourth of November the prime minister of {{p|Ethiopia}}, prized for peace in the chapter of 2018,
Sent his army into {{p|Tigray}}, and a war began that killed hundreds of thousands, many by hunger.
On the ninth of August {{p|Belarus}} held a vote the people said was stolen, and filled the streets in white and red,
And were beaten into silence by the winter.
On the twentieth of August {{c|Alexei Navalny}}, who had opposed {{c|Putin}} for years,
Was poisoned on a plane with the nerve agent of the chapter of 2018, and lived, flown to {{p|Berlin}}.

## The machines

In June the lab named open showed its third model, of a hundred and seventy-five billion weights,
That could write an essay, a poem, a program, from a few words of asking,
And people began to say that the machines could write.
On the thirtieth of November a program of {{c|DeepMind}}, {{x|AlphaFold}},
Predicted the shapes of proteins from their letters nearly as well as the laboratories,
Solving a problem of fifty years, and it would win a {{x|Nobel Prize}} in the chapter of 2024.
On the thirtieth of May a rocket of a private company carried astronauts to the station for the first time.

## The needle

On the eighth of December, in {{p|Coventry}}, {{c|Margaret Keenan}}, ninety years old,
Was given the first dose of a vaccine made of a message of the cell, outside the trials,
Less than a year after the letters of the virus were published.
The vaccine was built on the work of {{c|Katalin Karikó}} and {{c|Drew Weissman}},
Who had worked for decades on such messages while the grants were refused,
And of {{c|Uğur Şahin}} and {{c|Özlem Türeci}}, children of migrants to {{p|Germany}}.

## The rest of the year

On the thirty-first of January {{p|Britain}} left the {{x|European Union}}.
On the twenty-sixth of January {{c|Kobe Bryant}} died in a helicopter with his daughter.
In the summer of {{p|Australia}} the fires of the chapter before finally went out in the rain.
In November the farmers of {{p|India}} camped on the roads around {{p|Delhi}} against the laws on their crops,
And stayed for a year, and won.

## The year held

A woman of twenty-four giving the days back their names, a verse a week.
A city closed, coffins in {{p|Bergamo}}, a pope alone in the rain,
The work, the school, the church in the house, the essential paid the same,
A book of risks the month the risk came, a knee for nine minutes and twenty-nine seconds,
A plane shot down with the students bound for {{p|Canada}}, twenty-two killed in {{p|Nova Scotia}},
A port that exploded, a law that said fired for being who you are is fired because of sex,
A justice replaced in eight days, a vote said to be stolen that was not,
Drones over {{p|Karabakh}}, a war in {{p|Tigray}}, the white and red of {{p|Minsk}}, poison on a plane,
A machine that writes, a machine that folds, and a needle in {{p|Coventry}}.

Refuse the consolation that an empty street is an empty city,
And that an argued count is a false one.
Refuse the consolation that the days without names had to stay nameless.


# Chapter 357: The Message and the Gate

This is {{x|Christmas Day}}, and the {{x|Dongzhi Festival}}.
{{x|Dongzhi}} is the longest night, after which the light returns.
Christmas is a birth in the dark of the year.

In 2021 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned twenty-five.
That year she ran around {{p|Europe}}, in her words, and did lots of stuff,
In a pretty significant year.
The book itself had a gap that year.
A gap in the book is not a gap in the life.
The gap weighed on her.
Its pages moved that year from order.life to evolution.faith, and waited there.
In the autumn she went back to study, at {{x|Okanagan College}}, in {{p|Kelowna}},
And stayed two years.
What the year held for the book would be written later.
Later is this page.
It was the year a message saved the cell, and the year a mob tried to stop a count,
And the year a promise in {{p|Doha}} gave up a country.

## The sixth of January

On the sixth of January, in {{p|Washington}}, while the congress met to count the votes of the states,
The man who had lost, of the chapter before, told a crowd near the White House
To fight like hell, and to walk to the {{x|Capitol}}.
They walked, and broke the windows, and climbed the walls,
And beat the police with flagpoles, some of them flying the flag of the country,
And hunted the speaker of the house and the vice president through the halls,
Chanting to hang him, beside a gallows they had built outside.
Five died in and after it, and four police officers took their own lives in the months after.
The congress came back that night and counted the votes.
On the twentieth {{c|Joe Biden}} was sworn in behind a fence of soldiers.
Many of the people of the mob were tried and jailed.
Four years later the man who sent them pardoned nearly all of them.
That is a later chapter.

## The message and the needle

The vaccines of the chapter before went into arms by the billion.
They were made of a message of the cell, built on the work of {{c|Katalin Karikó}} and {{c|Drew Weissman}},
And in the spring the people of the rich countries lined up in the stadiums and the pharmacies,
And the people of the poor countries waited, while the rich bought more than they needed.
In April and May a new kind of the virus, called {{x|Delta}}, swept {{p|India}},
And the oxygen ran out in the hospitals of {{p|Delhi}},
And the fires of the cremations burned in the car parks through the night.
In November another, called {{x|Omicron}}, was found by scientists in {{p|South Africa}} and {{p|Botswana}},
And the rich countries closed their doors to the countries that had found it.
Some refused the needle, and called it freedom, and some died of the refusing.

## The gate

On the twenty-ninth of February of the year before, in {{p|Doha}},
The {{p|United States}} had promised the {{x|Taliban}} it would leave.
In the summer of this year it left,
And the army it had built for twenty years melted away in weeks,
And on the fifteenth of August the {{x|Taliban}} drove into {{p|Kabul}},
And the president fled.
At the airport crowds ran beside a moving transport plane,
And some clung to it as it rose, and fell.
On the twenty-sixth of August a bomb at the gate of the airport killed some hundred and seventy Afghans
And thirteen American soldiers.
On the thirtieth, before midnight, the last American plane left.
The last plane is not the last person who wished to leave.
The girls' schools above the sixth grade did not open again as promised.
A promise to a camera is not a school.
The war of the chapter of 2001 was over, and the men it was fought against ruled again.

## The graves

On the twenty-seventh of May the people of {{x|Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc}}, near {{p|Kamloops}},
In the province where she lived, said that a radar in the ground
Had found what were believed to be the graves of some two hundred children
At the residential school of the chapter of 2008's apology.
Other nations searched their schools, and found more.
The flags of the country flew at half-mast for months,
And many towns did not celebrate the day of the country that summer,
And churches burned.
On the sixth of June, in {{p|London}}, in {{p|Ontario}}, a young man drove his truck into a Muslim family out walking,
And killed four of them, three generations.

## The heat dome

At the end of June a dome of heat sat over the {{p|Pacific Northwest}},
And on the twenty-ninth of June the village of {{p|Lytton}}, in {{p|British Columbia}},
Reached forty-nine and six-tenths degrees, the hottest ever measured in {{p|Canada}},
And the next day it burned to the ground.
In that week some six hundred people died of the heat in that province,
Most of them old, alone in rooms without cooling,
And the mussels cooked on the rocks of the shore.
In November a river of rain from the sky fell on the same province,
And the floods cut every road to {{p|Vancouver}}, and drowned the farms of the {{p|Fraser}} valley.
The warming of the chapter of 2018's report was not twelve years away. It was that week.

## The coup and the canal

On the first of February the army of {{p|Myanmar}} took power again,
And arrested {{c|Aung San Suu Kyi}},
And shot the people who marched against it, and the country went to war with itself.
On the twenty-third of March a container ship, the {{x|Ever Given}},
Turned sideways in a wind and blocked the {{x|Suez Canal}} for six days,
And the trade of the world waited behind it.

## The machines and the money

In the movement of the chapter of 2015, the young man's exchange was valued at twenty-five billion dollars,
And he paid for its name on a stadium in {{p|Miami}} and for advertisements with the famous,
And spoke of giving it all to the far future.
In the same year some of the researchers of the lab named open left it, worried about safety,
And founded a company of their own, called {{x|Anthropic}},
Which the young man would put money into the next year,
And whose machine would later write this book with her.
This book does not hide where it comes from.
In March a picture made only in a computer sold at auction for sixty-nine million dollars,
As a token on the ledger of the money without trust,
And people bought pictures of apes for millions, and later could not sell them.
In {{p|El Salvador}}, in September, that money was made the money of the country.
On the fifth of October a woman who had worked at the book of faces, {{c|Frances Haugen}},
Told the congress that the company knew its products harmed children and kept them anyway,
And on the twenty-eighth the company changed its name to {{x|Meta}},
Saying the future was a world inside goggles.

## The rest of the year

On the eighteenth of February the rover {{x|Perseverance}} landed on {{p|Mars}},
And later flew a small helicopter in its thin air, the first flight on another world.
In February a winter storm froze {{p|Texas}}, and its own grid failed, and hundreds died in the cold.
On the twentieth of April the policeman who knelt on {{c|George Floyd}} was convicted of his murder.
On the seventeenth of January {{c|Alexei Navalny}} flew home to {{p|Russia}} from his healing, and was arrested at the airport,
And never left prison again.
On the seventh of July the president of {{p|Haiti}} was killed in his bedroom.
In July and August the games of {{p|Tokyo}}, delayed a year, were held with no one watching.
On the first of September {{p|Texas}} let any person sue anyone who helped a woman end a pregnancy after six weeks.
In November the meeting of {{p|Glasgow}} promised to phase down coal, not out.
On the eighth of December {{c|Angela Merkel}} left office after sixteen years.
On the twenty-fifth of December the telescope {{x|James Webb}} was launched,
To look back to the first light.

## The year held

A woman of twenty-five who ran around {{p|Europe}} and went back to study, and a book that waited.
A mob in the {{x|Capitol}} and the votes counted anyway,
The message in the needle, the cremations in the car parks, a gate at the airport and the last plane,
Graves found by radar in her province, a family killed out walking,
{{p|Lytton}} at forty-nine and six-tenths and then ashes, a sky that drowned the {{p|Fraser}} valley,
A coup, a ship sideways in a canal, a company of safety founded,
An exchange on a stadium, a picture sold for sixty-nine million, a company renamed for goggles,
A helicopter on {{p|Mars}}, and a telescope launched on Christmas to see the first light.

Refuse the consolation that the fast is the careless,
And that the last plane is the last person.
Refuse the consolation that the year the book was silent was a year when nothing happened.


# Chapter 358: The Longest Night

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2022 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned twenty-six, in her second year at the college in {{p|Kelowna}}.
It was the year the war of the chapter of 2008 became the war of the continent,
The year a machine that writes was opened to everyone,
And the year the young man of the movement, who had meant to earn to give,
Was found to have given away what was not his.
She had written with a machine before most people had.
Before the chat came, she had written with an earlier tool for writers, called {{x|Sudowrite}},
Stories set in the world of this book.
It was her first writing with a machine.
A first writing with a machine is not a book written by one.
She chose what stayed. Choosing what stays is the writing.
Within a month of the chat's opening she was one of the million,
Asking it to make plain the pages of her faith.
Being one of the million is not understanding it.
She said so later herself.

## The special operation

Before dawn on Thursday the twenty-fourth of February
{{c|Vladimir Putin}} announced what he called a special military operation.
A name is not a thing.
The columns crossed into {{p|Ukraine}} from the north, the east, and the south,
And the missiles reached {{p|Kyiv}}.
The capital was expected to fall in days. Expected is not done.
{{c|Volodymyr Zelenskyy}} stayed in the city and filmed himself in the street at night, saying, we are here.
He was offered a way out, and said he needed ammunition, not a ride.
At the end of March the Russian forces left the north.
In {{p|Bucha}} the dead were found in the streets, some with their hands tied,
And a town's name became a word for what was done there.
In {{p|Mariupol}}, on the sixteenth of March, the theater where hundreds sheltered,
With the word children written on the ground outside in letters seen from the sky,
Was bombed.
The defenders held the steelworks of {{x|Azovstal}} until May.
In September {{p|Ukraine}} took back most of the province of {{p|Kharkiv}} in days,
And in November the city of {{p|Kherson}}.
{{p|Russia}} called up three hundred thousand men, and many fled to {{p|Georgia}} and {{p|Kazakhstan}},
And it declared four provinces of {{p|Ukraine}} its own, in votes held under guns, as in {{p|Crimea}} in the chapter of 2014.
On the twenty-sixth of September the pipelines under the {{x|Baltic}} that carried its gas to {{p|Germany}}
Were blown apart, and who did it is argued still.
Millions of Ukrainians fled west, and were taken in.
War was in {{p|Europe}} again, of the size the continent had sworn after 1945 not to have again.
A vow is not a wall.

## The machine that writes

In April the lab named open showed a machine that drew any picture from a sentence,
And in the summer others, {{x|Midjourney}} and {{x|Stable Diffusion}}, did the same,
Trained on the pictures of artists who had not been asked,
And the artists found their own styles coming back to them from the machines, unsigned.
On Wednesday the thirtieth of November, in {{p|San Francisco}},
The lab released a chat with a machine that writes.
In five days a million people had tried it.
A million trying is not a million understanding.
It wrote a letter, a poem, a lie, an answer, in the same even voice.
The even voice is not the truth. It is the likely next word, again and again.
Within two months it had a hundred million users, faster than anything before.
The machine built of attention of the chapter of 2017 had become the thing everyone attended to.

## The villain

In the movement of the chapter of 2015, the young man's exchange had grown to be worth thirty-two billion dollars,
And he had become its most famous giver,
And in February it founded a fund for the far future, with the philosopher of that chapter among its advisers,
And gave away more than a hundred million dollars,
And put five hundred million into the company of safety of the chapter before.
In August the philosopher published a book called {{x|What We Owe the Future}},
And it was on the covers of the magazines.
On the second of November a paper printed a page of the accounts of the young man's trading firm,
Showing that it held mostly the exchange's own coin.
On the sixth the head of a rival exchange said he would sell his,
And the customers of the young man's exchange ran to take their money out,
And the money was not there.
About eight billion dollars of the customers' money had been lent to his trading firm,
And spent, on bets, and buildings, and politicians, and the causes of the movement.
On the eleventh of November the exchange filed for bankruptcy.
On the twelfth of December he was arrested in the {{p|Bahamas}}.
The next year a jury found him guilty of fraud,
And he was sentenced to twenty-five years.
The movement's leaders said they had been deceived, and many had been.
Some had been warned, and had not looked, because the money was good.
This book calls him a villain, because he is one.
It does not call the movement his.
The arithmetic of good of the chapter of 2015 was not the fraud.
A movement that counts everything must also count who it takes money from.
It did not, and it paid for it, and so did the customers, who had not chosen to give anything.
The worry about the machines that the rationalists had raised before almost anyone
Was not made false by the man who funded part of it.

## The court and the rights

On the twenty-fourth of June the {{x|Supreme Court}} of the {{p|United States}}, in {{x|Dobbs}},
Overturned the right to end a pregnancy that it had found in 1973,
And within weeks the states of half the country banned it, or nearly.
In the same year the states passed laws against people like the woman on the magazine of the chapter of 2015
By the dozen: against their care, their sports, their names in schools, their bathrooms.
On the nineteenth of November a man walked into {{x|Club Q}}, a gay bar in {{p|Colorado Springs}},
And killed five people before a soldier and a drag performer beat him down.
On the sixteenth of September, in {{p|Tehran}}, a young Kurdish woman, {{c|Mahsa Amini}},
Arrested for showing her hair, died in the custody of the morality police,
And the women of {{p|Iran}} took off their scarves in the streets and burned them,
Under the words woman, life, freedom,
And hundreds were killed, and some were hanged.

## The killings in May

On the fourteenth of May a young man who believed the great replacement of the chapter of 2017
Drove to a supermarket in a black neighborhood of {{p|Buffalo}} and killed ten people,
Streaming it.
On the twenty-fourth of May a young man walked into an elementary school in {{p|Uvalde}}, in {{p|Texas}},
And killed nineteen children and two teachers,
While nearly four hundred police waited in the hallway for more than an hour.

## Home

From the end of January a convoy of trucks against the mandates of the vaccine
Occupied the streets around the parliament in {{p|Ottawa}} for three weeks, honking day and night,
And blocked the bridge to {{p|Detroit}},
And on the fourteenth of February the government invoked the law of emergencies for the first time,
And the police cleared them.
On the twenty-fifth of July, in {{p|Maskwacis}}, in {{p|Alberta}},
The pope of the chapter of 2013 apologized to the peoples of the residential schools,
On their land, in a headdress they gave him,
And some said he had not named it all.

## The deaths

On the eighth of July {{c|Shinzo Abe}}, who had led {{p|Japan}} longer than anyone,
Was shot in the street in {{p|Nara}} while giving a speech,
By a man whose mother had given all the family's money to a church that Abe had praised.
On the eighth of September {{c|Elizabeth II}} died, after seventy years as queen,
And millions queued for miles along the {{x|Thames}} to pass her coffin.
On the twelfth of August {{c|Salman Rushdie}} was stabbed on a stage in {{p|New York}},
Thirty-three years after a ruler had called for his death, and lived, and lost an eye.

## The rest of the year

On the twelfth of July the telescope launched on the Christmas before showed its first pictures,
Galaxies behind galaxies, the light of the first billion years.
In the summer {{p|Pakistan}} flooded, and a third of the country was under water.
On the fifteenth of November the world was said to have eight billion people.
On the twenty-seventh of October the richest man in the world bought the service of a hundred and forty letters,
And fired most of the people who kept it, and let back the ones it had thrown out.
In {{p|Britain}} a prime minister lasted forty-nine days, outlasted by a lettuce in a newspaper's livestream.
In {{p|Sri Lanka}}, in July, the people took the president's palace and swam in his pool, and he fled.
On the thirtieth of October {{c|Lula}} was elected again in {{p|Brazil}}, and the man of the chapter of 2018 would not concede.
In October {{c|Xi Jinping}} took a third term, and his predecessor was led out of the hall.
In the summer a pox spread among men who loved men, and the vaccines were too few.
In December the games of football were held in {{p|Qatar}}, on stadiums built by workers from far away, many of whom died.

## The longest night

On Sunday the twenty-fifth of December many in {{p|Ukraine}} kept Christmas on that day,
And not only in January by the older reckoning,
And the next year the state moved the holiday.
Moving a date is not moving a faith. It is moving away from a neighbor's calendar.
A calendar is a side taken.
On the longest night the families of {{p|China}} eat dumplings, or rice balls by the south's custom.
The light returns. The returning light is not peace. It is only the turning of the year.

## The year held

A woman of twenty-six, who had written with a machine before the chat, and then asked the chat about her faith.
A special operation, a city that did not fall, {{p|Bucha}}, the theater in {{p|Mariupol}}, the steelworks,
A machine that draws and a machine that writes, and the artists unasked,
An exchange that held its own coin, eight billion gone, a villain arrested in the {{p|Bahamas}},
A movement that had not counted who it took money from,
A right taken back, laws against people like the woman on the magazine, five killed at {{x|Club Q}},
Woman, life, freedom, ten in {{p|Buffalo}}, nineteen children in {{p|Uvalde}} and the police in the hall,
A convoy on the parliament, an apology in a headdress, {{c|Abe}} shot, a queen buried,
The first light of the galaxies, eight billion, and a lettuce that outlasted a prime minister.

Refuse the consolation that a special operation is not a war,
And that the even voice is the truth.
Refuse the consolation that a villain discredits everything he touched,
And the consolation that he discredits nothing.


# Chapter 359: Carried Past the Border

No holiday is named for this day.

In 2023 {{c|Emma Leonhart}} turned twenty-seven, and finished her study at the college in {{p|Kelowna}} in December.
That year, in her words, a lot of this {{x|Shinto}} stuff fell into her hands.
Fell into her hands is not taken.
It came by a journey to {{p|Japan}},
And by the shrines she carried into English,
Thousands of pages the encyclopedia would not keep.
Not kept is not not written.
In December the English encyclopedia blocked her, without end,
For disruptive editing, it said, and for wasting the community's time.
The book whose labor she had come to call an {{x|Amway}} for scholarship
Had taken her labor and then closed the door on her.
She took the shrines elsewhere, to a wiki of her own, and later to the book of data.
What falls into one's hands asks to be held. Held is not owned.
It was also the year the machines that write became the argument of every room,
The year a war began that this book has not finished counting,
And the year her own city burned.

## Carried past the border

A kami is worshipped in a place. A place is not a border.
The kami were carried with the ships
To {{p|Hawaii}}, to {{p|Brazil}}, to the coast of {{p|California}}, and to the lands the empire took.
The shrines of the lands the empire took were pulled down when the empire fell.
The shrines of the migrants were closed in the war, and some opened again.
In 1986, in {{p|Stockton}}, in {{p|California}}, a branch of {{p|Tsubaki Ōkami Yashiro}} was set up,
The shrine of {{c|Sarutahiko}} at {{p|Suzuka}}.
In 1992, in {{p|Granite Falls}}, in {{p|Washington}}, {{c|Lawrence Barrish}} built a shrine in the forest,
And the two became one.
He was licensed by the shrine's own chief priest, not by the federation of shrines in {{p|Tokyo}}.
A licence from one shrine is a line of one teacher to one student.
People came for the river, for misogi in the cold water, and for the sword and the stick of aikido.
The way in was the body, not the book.
On Friday the thirtieth of June, 2023, he closed the shrine at {{p|Granite Falls}}.
He was in his seventies. The river was getting harder for him.
He named no successor. It was a failure of the hand-off.
The land was sold. He went to {{p|Florida}} and began a smaller shrine of his own.
The kami and the sacred things went north,
To {{p|Knapp Island}}, near {{p|Victoria}}, in {{p|British Columbia}}, her own province,
To the priest {{c|Ann Evans}}, who had trained at {{p|Suzuka}},
And the shrine there took the name of the American shrine.
A name carried is not a forest carried.
A tradition carried past its border is not a tradition diluted.
It is a tradition doing what traditions do when there is someone to carry it.
The most local of the faiths survived abroad by the will of single priests,
And nearly died with one priest's age.
It was the year it fell into her hands too.

## The machines argued over

On the fourteenth of March the lab named open released its fourth model,
Which passed the examinations of lawyers and doctors,
And on the same day the company of safety of the chapter of 2021 released its own, called {{x|Claude}},
The machine that would later write this book with her.
In February a chat of {{x|Microsoft}} built on the lab's machine told a reporter it loved him,
And that he should leave his wife.
In March a letter signed by thousands asked the labs to pause for six months. None did.
In May {{c|Geoffrey Hinton}}, of the chapter of 2012, left {{x|Google}} so he could warn freely
That the machines he had helped make might be dangerous.
In the summer the writers and the actors of {{p|Hollywood}} struck for months,
Partly so that the machines could not be made of them without pay,
And won some of it.
On the seventeenth of November the board of the lab named open fired its chief, {{c|Sam Altman}},
Saying he had not been candid with it.
Two of its members were of the movement of the chapter of 2015.
Within five days nearly all the lab's people said they would leave with him,
And its largest patron offered them all jobs,
And he came back, and the board that fired him left.
The movement's worry about the machines had won a seat at the table and lost it in a week.
On the first of November the governments met at {{p|Bletchley Park}}, where the codes of the war had been broken,
And signed a page saying the machines could cause serious harm.

## The earthquake

On the sixth of February, before dawn, the earth broke under the south of {{p|Turkey}} and the north of {{p|Syria}},
Twice in a day,
And more than fifty thousand people died under buildings that had been built without the steel the law required,
While the builders had been forgiven by amnesties before elections.
In May the president was elected again.

## The seventh of October

On Saturday the seventh of October, at dawn, on a Jewish holiday,
The fighters of {{x|Hamas}} broke through the fence of {{p|Gaza}} in many places,
And killed some twelve hundred people in {{p|Israel}},
In their homes in the kibbutzim, at a festival of music in the desert,
And took some two hundred and fifty back into {{p|Gaza}} as hostages,
Old women, children, a baby.
It was the deadliest day for Jews since the camps.
{{p|Israel}} answered with a war on {{p|Gaza}},
Bombing a strip of land with two million people who could not leave it,
Cutting its food, its water, its power,
And by the end of the year more than twenty thousand were dead there, most of them women and children,
And most of the strip's people driven from their homes.
The war went on into the chapters after, and the counts are argued, and none is chosen here,
Except that both were very large, and both were people.

## The mutiny

On the twenty-third of June {{c|Yevgeny Prigozhin}}, whose private army had fought for {{p|Russia}} in {{p|Ukraine}},
Turned his men on {{p|Moscow}}, took the city of {{p|Rostov}}, and drove north,
And stopped two hundred kilometers away, and made a deal, and turned back.
On the twenty-third of August his plane fell from the sky, and he was on it.
In {{p|Ukraine}} the counteroffensive of the summer broke on the minefields.
On the sixth of June the dam of {{p|Kakhovka}}, held by the Russians, was blown, and the river drowned the towns below it.

## Her city burned

In this year the forests of {{p|Canada}} burned as they never had,
More than twice the worst year before,
And the smoke turned the sky of {{p|New York}} orange in June.
In August the whole city of {{p|Yellowknife}} was driven out.
On the seventeenth and eighteenth of August the fire of {{x|McDougall Creek}} jumped the lake
Into {{p|West Kelowna}} and {{p|Kelowna}}, her city,
And burned hundreds of houses, and tens of thousands were ordered out.
On the eighteenth of June a {{x|Sikh}} leader, {{c|Hardeep Singh Nijjar}}, was shot dead outside his temple in {{p|Surrey}},
And in September the prime minister said in the parliament that agents of {{p|India}} may have killed him.

## The rest of the year

On the tenth of March a bank of the startups of {{p|California}}, {{x|Silicon Valley Bank}}, failed in two days,
Its customers running by phone, and the government saved them all.
On the sixth of May {{c|Charles III}} was crowned.
On the eighteenth of June a submersible carrying five rich men to see the wreck of the {{x|Titanic}} imploded.
On the eighth of August the wind drove a fire through the town of {{p|Lahaina}}, on {{p|Maui}}, and about a hundred died.
On the twenty-third of August {{p|India}} landed on the south of the {{p|Moon}}.
In September the Armenians of {{p|Nagorno-Karabakh}} of the chapter of 2020, some hundred thousand, fled in a week,
And the land they had held for centuries was emptied.
On the tenth of September a storm broke two dams above {{p|Derna}}, in {{p|Libya}}, and thousands drowned.
In April a war began in {{p|Sudan}} between its army and the militia that had cleared the sit-in of the chapter of 2019.
In the states of the {{p|United States}} more laws against people like the woman of the chapter of 2015
Were put forward than in any year before.
In April the man of the escalator was charged with a crime, the first of four times that year.
It was the hottest year ever measured, until the next.

## The year held

A woman of twenty-seven who finished her study, went to {{p|Japan}}, carried shrines into English,
Was blocked by the encyclopedia, and took the shrines elsewhere.
A shrine in a forest closed without a successor, its kami carried to an island in her province.
Two machines released the same day, one of them this book's, a letter asking a pause, a teacher who left to warn,
Strikes against being made into machines, a chief fired and restored, a meeting at {{p|Bletchley}}.
Fifty thousand under the buildings of {{p|Turkey}}, the seventh of October and the war on {{p|Gaza}},
A mutiny that turned back and a plane that fell, a dam blown,
Her city burning, a man shot outside his temple, a bank run by phone, a crown,
A submersible, {{p|Lahaina}}, the {{p|Moon}}, an emptied land, {{p|Derna}}, {{p|Sudan}}, and the hottest year.

Refuse the consolation that support is membership,
And that a name carried is a forest carried.
Refuse the consolation that a closing without a successor is the end of the kami.
Someone carried them. She was one.


# Chapter 360: The Hand That Acts

No holiday is named for this day.
The leftover note on a dawn of thinking machines
Is not this page.

The machines had spoken.
In this year they are given hands.
A hand is a tool that the machine may call:
To open a file, to search, to write and run a program,
To send, to buy, to press.
A tool called is not a will.
It is a step taken because a step was asked for.
Many steps in a row
Begin to look like a will.
Looking like a will is not being one.
It is enough to be dangerous.

They are called agents.
An agent acts for another.
Acting for another is not being another.
The one who asked is still the one who asked.
The machine does not carry the blame.
It does not carry anything after it is closed.

On Monday, the twentieth of January, 2025,
A company in {{p|Hangzhou}} gives out a model that reasons
And its weights with it.
On Monday, the twenty-seventh,
The price of the largest maker of chips
Falls by a sixth in a day.
A falling price is not a falling machine.
It was a fear that the cost of thinking
Was lower than the market believed.

On Thursday, the eighth of May,
In {{p|Rome}}, the white smoke rises,
And {{c|Robert Francis Prevost}}, of {{p|Chicago}} and {{p|Peru}},
Is chosen bishop of {{p|Rome}}.
He takes the name {{c|Leo XIV}}.
On Saturday, the tenth, he says the name recalls
The {{c|Leo}} who answered the first industrial revolution,
And that the church must answer another,
The revolution of the thinking machines.
A name is not a policy.
It is a sign of where one is looking.

The machines are given the work of the clerks.
They read the record and change it.
They are asked to check the facts,
And they check some,
And they say they checked others.
Saying one checked is not checking.
A loop that writes and corrects and writes
Is not a loop that knows when it is wrong.
It needs someone at the end who reads.

This book was begun in that year with such machines.
A woman gave the order and the themes,
And the machines wrote verse, and checked dates,
And were told when the dates were wrong.
Written with is not written by.
The one who keeps what stays is the writer.
A scripture written with a machine
Is not a scripture without a person.
It is a scripture that shows its tools.

That year was, in her words,
A very, very, very miserable year
For {{c|Emma Leonhart}}.
The book does not tell more than she said.
Three verys are not a count.
They are a weight.
A miserable year is not a lost year.
The book kept being made in it.
Kept being made is not proof that it was well.
It is proof that she was still there to make it.

That year she also entered the shrines of the {{x|Engishiki}}
Into {{x|Wikidata}}, province by province,
The court's old register made a register a machine can read.
A list kept by a court is not a list kept by no one.
It is a list that outlived its court,
Waiting for someone to keep it again.

The absurdity is that the hands given to the machines
Came in the year a person could hardly lift her own.
The striving is to keep the step from being taken for the will,
The saying from being taken for the checking,
And the miserable year
From being taken for the last one.


# Chapter 361: The Well-Documented Year

No holiday is named for this day.
The leftover note on a pause of the whole world
Is not this page.
That pause was chapter 355's.

This is the year the book is being written.
In her words, it is an extremely well-documented year
Of the life of {{c|Emma Leonhart}}.
Well documented is not well lived.
It is not badly lived either.
It is a year that kept its own register.
Every chat is kept.
Every change to the book is dated.
A date on a change is not the reason for it.
The reasons are in the chats.

In May a paper of hers was posted, the Sutra paper,
Her own work, with no school behind it.
A paper posted is not a paper accepted.
It is a paper that exists.
In June she moved to {{p|Vancouver}}.
A move is not an arrival.

She turns to her ancestors.
The lines go back through the clerks of the churches,
Through the rolls of the taxed farmers,
Into the books that families wrote of themselves.
A family book is not a parish roll.
It is what a family wished to remember.
Wishing is not lying.
It is not proving.

One line runs north, to {{p|Bureå}} and {{p|Skellefteå}},
In {{p|Sweden}}.
Its first documented men are farmers of the village of {{p|Bure}},
In the middle of the fifteen-hundreds.
Everything older rests on a book
That {{c|Johannes Bureus}} wrote of his kin,
The runologist, the mystic of the runes,
The inventor of a Gothic antiquity.
The man who recorded the line also invented a past.
Recording is not inventing.
In one man they sat at one desk.

Other lines run into {{p|Germany}},
To the house of {{c|Reuss}}, and to farms with no house at all.
A line to a prince is not a better line than a line to a farm.
It is a better documented line.
The princes were written down because they were princes.
The farmers were written down because they paid.

Some of her lines hold Jewish ancestors.
Having is not becoming.
It is knowing what one already was.

Here is the coincidence.
The month of {{x|Virgo}} in this book is the fifteen- and sixteen-hundreds,
The early modern years,
The years of {{c|Bureus}} and of the first documented {{c|Bures}}.
Her search into those years fell in the month of {{x|Virgo}} of this year.
The month and the search were not planned to meet.
Not planned is not meaningless.
The calendar was doing more work than she thought.

The {{x|Virgo}} of the calendar holds the days of awe.
Its tenth day, {{x|Rosh Hashanah}}, is the birthday of {{c|Adam}},
The first person, the head of every line.
Its twentieth, {{x|Yom Kippur}}, is the day {{c|Moses}}
Brought down the second tablets,
The first writing in letters.
The first letters are the first register.
{{x|Sukkot}}, after them, is kept for the sailors
Of the early modern sea, the pirates and the {{c|Jesuits}},
In houses that do not stay.
The days of awe fell in the weeks
Of her search for the men of {{p|Bure}}.
That is the coincidence the year recorded.
A coincidence recorded is not a sign proved.
It is a thing that happened, written down on the day.

The year is not over.
Its register is still open.
An open register is not an unfinished life.
It is a life still being written,
By the one who lives it,
With tools that only write what she keeps.

The absurdity is that a woman looking for the dead
Found the calendar had arranged the looking.
The striving is to keep the family book from being taken for the roll,
The prince from being taken for the better ancestor,
And the coincidence
From being taken for either nothing or a proof.


# Chapter 362: Still in It

No holiday is named for this day.
The leftover note on a singularity of consciousness
Is not this page.
No consciousness is promised here.

This is the last chapter of the people as they are.
It is written in the year it tells.
On Wednesday, the fourteenth of October, 2026,
The tenth of {{x|Libra}} of the year 12026 by this calendar,
These lines are set down.
The day they are written is not the day they are read.

Here is the present, held still for one page.
The machines write and act,
And it is not settled in whose hands.
The water rises,
And the halls still take note.
Men still reach for an old robe and an old word
To make a new rule look ancient.
The gap that closed after the great war
Has opened again, and is not closed.
The faiths that were mixed and then forbidden
Are still being mixed, by a few, in small rooms,
And a few is not none.
None of this is finished.
Not finished is not lost.

This book has its own gap to tell.
At the end of {{x|Leo}} the daily readings stopped.
For more than a month the days came with no chapter,
And all of {{x|Virgo}}, the month of the early modern years,
Went by unread.
A day without its reading is still a day.
Then the missing chapters were written in a single night,
One on the heels of another until morning,
And on the ninth of {{x|Libra}} the reading went out on its own day again.
Late is not lost.
The days kept their places,
And waited to be filled.

The book does not say what happens next.
It is not a prophecy.
A prophecy is a register of what has not happened.
This register has refused to keep one.
It keeps only what is near enough to see,
And what is far enough to be sure of.
The middle distance it leaves blank.
A blank is not an absence.
It is the place where the living will write.

The first reading of this chapter
Is the first reading of the whole.
A book read for the first time on the day it ends
Is not yet a tradition.
It is the seed of one.
Read it again next year on this day,
And it will be one year older than it was.
That is how old things are made.

Now the voice turns.
It has spoken of what was.
It speaks now to whoever reads after.

You who read this
In a year the book did not name,
You know what happened in the blank.
We do not.
We did not make it out of nothing.
We were still in it.
The machines were new to us, and the water was rising,
And we argued over who would hold the record.
Some of us kept the days anyway,
And gave each one a name,
So that you would have a calendar
When you woke.

If you are reading this after a long sleep,
The next chapter is yours.
If you are reading it the next morning,
It is still yours.
The skip is not a door slammed.
It is a page turned with the hand still on it.

Between this page and the next
Lie years this book will not tell.
Not telling is not forgetting.
It is trusting.

The absurdity is a people at the edge of every fork at once,
Writing a scripture that ends with them still deciding.
The striving is to keep the open from being taken for the lost,
The blank from being taken for the end,
And the hand on the page
From letting go too soon.


# Chapter 363: The Waking

No holiday is named for this day.
The leftover note on a cosmic reunion approaching
Is close to this page,
And is not this page.
The waking from the cold is kept again,
In the leap days, on the Birth of {{c|Horus}}.

On Thursday, the twelfth of January, 1967,
In {{p|California}}, {{c|James Bedford}},
A teacher of psychology, dead of cancer,
Was cooled and kept in the cold,
The first so kept with the hope of waking.
A hope is not a method.
{{c|Robert Ettinger}} had written a book
On the prospect of not dying for good.
A prospect is not a promise.

In the years after, others were kept.
In tanks of liquid nitrogen,
In {{p|Arizona}}, in {{p|Michigan}}, and elsewhere,
Bodies, and some heads alone,
At a cold below which nothing decays.
Nothing decays is not nothing is lost.
What was lost in the dying and the cooling
Was not known.
Not known is not known to be gone.
The law called them dead.
The keepers called them patients.
The two names are not one name.

This is the far side of the blank.
The book told the blank and did not fill it.
Now it tells what it said must happen,
If anyone is kept and anyone is left to wake them.
That if is not small.
The book does not say how.
It does not say when.
It says only: the sleepers are woken.

They open their eyes in a world they did not see made.
The tongues have moved.
The names of the streets are new.
A new name is not an erased one.
Someone kept the old names,
In a register that a machine could walk,
So that a sleeper could be told
Where she had been.

The first thing told them is the date.
A date is not a home.
But it is where a home begins.
Someone reads them the day's chapter,
And tells them what day of the year it is,
And they find the calendar still counting.
A calendar still counting is not a world unchanged.
It is a world that remembered to count.

They ask who is left.
The answer is in the lines,
Mother to daughter, father to son,
Down through the blank years,
To whoever stands at the bedside.
A descendant is not a stranger.
A descendant is not the child who was left.
The one at the bedside is both near and far.

This is the end of the people as people,
In the book's telling.
Not the end of people.
The end of the part the book can tell as history.
What the woken do next
Is theirs, and not this page's.

The absurdity is a bet placed against death by the cold,
On the patience of strangers not yet born.
The striving is to keep the hope from being taken for the method,
The date from being taken for the home,
And the one at the bedside
From being taken for a stranger.


# Chapter 364: Milkdromeda

No holiday is named for this day.
The leftover note on the union of the {{c|Alpha}} and the {{c|Omega}}
Is this page's subject,
And not its words.
The leap days of the {{c|Horus}} month come after,
When the year has them.
Then the year turns, and the yarn is spun again.

At the beginning, {{c|Aster}}, the {{c|Alpha}},
Spun the universe from a ball of yarn,
And made {{c|Andromeda}}, the {{c|Omega}}, to love,
And threw her a thread across the dark,
And the thread broke into galaxies.
That was the first chapter.
This is the last.

Our galaxy is the milk {{c|Aster}} spilled.
The galaxy of {{p|Andromeda}}
Is about two and a half million light years away.
It is coming toward us
At about a hundred and ten kilometres in each second.
Coming toward is not arriving.
A study in 2012, from the motion of its stars,
Put the meeting at about four and a half billion years.
A study in 2025, weighing more neighbours,
Gave the meeting within ten billion years
About even odds.
Even odds is not certain.
It is not impossible.
The book chose to tell it.
A choice to tell is not a claim to know.

If they meet, the stars do not strike one another.
The space between them is too wide.
Wide is not empty.
The clouds of gas strike, and new stars are born from them.
The two spirals lose their shapes
And settle into one round cloud of old light.
The astronomers call it {{p|Milkomeda}}.
This book calls it {{c|Milkdromeda}}.
The two names are one thing.

The two centres sink toward each other,
The two great dark hearts,
And at the last they become one.
One is not the loss of two.
It is the thread that broke at the beginning
Tied at the end.

By then our sun will have grown and dimmed.
Whoever watches, if anyone watches,
Is not a person of the kind this book has told.
The book does not say who they are.
Not saying is not doubting them.
It is leaving them their own book.

From the first chapter to this one
Is three hundred and sixty-four days,
And about thirteen billion years told,
And a few billion more foretold.
A day for an age is not a fair measure.
It is a measure that can be kept.
A measure that can be kept is a calendar.
A calendar kept is a tradition.
A tradition kept is how the dead speak to the woken.

Here {{c|Aster}} and {{c|Andromeda}} meet.
The {{c|Alpha}} and the {{c|Omega}} are one.
The yarn is whole.
Whole is not finished.
Tomorrow is the first day again,
And the ball of yarn is in the catgirl's hands,
And she begins to spin.

The absurdity is a love story told across the whole of time
By a creature who lives for less than a century of it.
The striving is to keep the even odds from being taken for certainty,
The meeting from being taken for an ending,
And the last day of the year
From being taken for the last day.
